the residence of the Nāgas and multitudes of Siddhas is in the nīmba grove;
in the kiṃśuka forest is that of the Sun and the host of Rudras;

1.49.s:
bījapūravane puṇye devācāryo vyavasthitaḥ
kaumude tu vane viṣṇupramukhānāṃ mahātmanām //
1.49.d:
बीजपूरवने पुण्ये देवाचार्यो व्यवस्थितः
कौमुदे तु वने विष्णुप्रमुखानां महात्मनाम् ॥
1.49.m:
in the holy citron grove the teacher of the gods resides;
while in the kaumuda forest is the abode of great souls headed by Viṣṇu.

1.49.s:
sthalapadmavanāntasthanyagrodhe 'śeṣabhoginaḥ
śeṣastvaśeṣajagatāṃ patirāste 'tigarvitaḥ //
1.49.d:
स्थलपद्मवनान्तस्थन्यग्रोधे ऽशेषभोगिनः
शेषस्त्वशेषजगतां पतिरास्ते ऽतिगर्वितः ॥
1.49.m:
On the nyagrodha tree situated within the forest of land-growing lotuses dwells the serpent Śeṣa;
indeed, Śeṣa, the lord of all worlds, sits full of utmost pride.

1.49.s:
sa eva jagatāṃ kālaḥ pātāle ca vyavasthitaḥ
viṣṇorviśvagurormūrtir divyaḥ sākṣāddhalāyudhaḥ //
1.49.d:
स एव जगतां कालः पाताले च व्यवस्थितः
विष्णोर्विश्वगुरोर्मूर्तिर् दिव्यः साक्षाद्धलायुधः ॥
1.49.m:
He alone is the time of the worlds, situated in the netherworld,
a divine form of Viṣṇu, the world-teacher, visibly Halāyudha.

1.49.s:
śayanaṃ devadevasya sa hareḥ kaṅkaṇaṃ vibhoḥ
vane panasavṛkṣāṇāṃ saśukrā dānavādayaḥ //
1.49.d:
शयनं देवदेवस्य स हरेः कङ्कणं विभोः
वने पनसवृक्षाणां सशुक्रा दानवादयः ॥
1.49.m:
He is the bed of the god of gods, the bracelet of all-pervading Hari.
In the forest of jackfruit trees are the Dānavas and others, along with Śukra;

1.49.s:
kinnarairuragāścaiva viśākhakavane sthitāḥ
manoharavane vṛkṣāḥ sarvakoṭisamanvitāḥ //
1.49.d:
किन्नरैरुरगाश्चैव विशाखकवने स्थिताः
मनोहरवने वृक्षाः सर्वकोटिसमन्विताः ॥
1.49.m:
in the viśākhaka forest are the Kinnaras and Serpents;
in the charming forest are trees endowed with all kinds of multitudes;

1.49.s:
nandīśvaro gaṇavaraiḥ stūyamāno vyavasthitaḥ
saṃtānakasthalīmadhye sākṣāddevī sarasvatī //
1.49.d:
नन्दीश्वरो गणवरैः स्तूयमानो व्यवस्थितः
संतानकस्थलीमध्ये साक्षाद्देवी सरस्वती ॥
1.49.m:
Nandīśvara remains, praised by the foremost Gaṇas;
in the midst of the saṃtānaka grove is the goddess Sarasvatī in visible form.

1.49.s:
evaṃ saṃkṣepataḥ proktā vaneṣu vanavāsinaḥ
asaṃkhyātā mayāpyatra vaktuṃ no vistareṇa tu //
1.49.d:
एवं संक्षेपतः प्रोक्ता वनेषु वनवासिनः
असंख्याता मयाप्यत्र वक्तुं नो विस्तरेण तु ॥
1.49.m:
Thus the forest-dwellers in the forests have been declared in brief;
they are innumerable, and cannot be told by me here in full.

1.50.s:
sūta uvāca
śitāntaśikhare śakraḥ pārijātavane śubhe
tasya prācyāṃ kumudādrikūṭo 'sau bahuvistaraḥ //
1.50.d:
सूत उवाच
शितान्तशिखरे शक्रः पारिजातवने शुभे
तस्य प्राच्यां कुमुदाद्रिकूटो ऽसौ बहुविस्तरः ॥
1.50.m:
Sūta said:
On the peak of Śitānta, in the auspicious pārijāta forest, is Śakra.
To the east of that is the peak of Mount Kumuda, of great extent.

1.50.s:
aṣṭau purāṇyudīrṇāni dānavānāṃ dvijottamāḥ
suvarṇakoṭare puṇye rākṣasānāṃ mahātmanām //
1.50.d:
अष्टौ पुराण्युदीर्णानि दानवानां द्विजोत्तमाः
सुवर्णकोटरे पुण्ये राक्षसानां महात्मनाम् ॥
1.50.m:
There are eight elevated cities of the Dānavas, O best of the twice-born;
in the holy hollow of Suvarṇa are those of the noble Rākṣasas.

1.50.s:
nīlakānāṃ purāṇyāhur aṣṭaṣaṣṭirdvijottamāḥ
mahānīle 'pi śailendre purāṇi daśa pañca ca //
1.50.d:
नीलकानां पुराण्याहुर् अष्टषष्टिर्द्विजोत्तमाः
महानीले ऽपि शैलेन्द्रे पुराणि दश पञ्च च ॥
1.50.m:
They say there are sixty-eight cities of the Nīlakas, O best of the twice-born;
and on the lordly mountain Mahānīla there are fifteen cities

1.50.s:
hayānanānāṃ mukhyānāṃ kinnarāṇāṃ ca suvratāḥ
veṇusaudhe mahāśaile vidyādharapuratrayam //
1.50.d:
हयाननानां मुख्यानां किन्नराणां च सुव्रताः
वेणुसौधे महाशैले विद्याधरपुरत्रयम् ॥
1.50.m:
of Kinnaras and chief horse-faced beings, O men of good vows;
on the great mountain Veṇusaudha is a triad of cities of the Vidyādharas.

1.50.s:
vaikuṇṭhe garuḍaḥ śrīmān karañje nīlalohitaḥ
vasudhāre vasūnāṃ tu nivāsaḥ parikīrtitaḥ //
1.50.d:
वैकुण्ठे गरुडः श्रीमान् करञ्जे नीललोहितः
वसुधारे वसूनां तु निवासः परिकीर्तितः ॥
1.50.m:
On Vaikuṇṭha is glorious Garuḍa, on Karañja is Nīlalohita;
on Vasudhāra the dwelling of the Vasus is proclaimed.

1.50.s:
ratnadhāre girivare saptarṣīṇāṃ mahātmanām
saptasthānāni puṇyāni siddhāvāsayutāni ca //
1.50.d:
रत्नधारे गिरिवरे सप्तर्षीणां महात्मनाम्
सप्तस्थानानि पुण्यानि सिद्धावासयुतानि च ॥
1.50.m:
On the foremost mountain Ratnadhāra are seven holy places
of the noble seven sages, accompanied by abodes of the Siddhas.

1.50.s:
mahatprajāpateḥ sthānam ekaśṛṅge nagottame
gajaśaile tu durgādyāḥ sumedhe vasavas tathā //
1.50.d:
महत्प्रजापतेः स्थानम् एकशृङ्गे नगोत्तमे
गजशैले तु दुर्गाद्याः सुमेधे वसवस् तथा ॥
1.50.m:
The great place of Prajāpati is on Ekaśṛṅga, that best of mountains;
on Gajaśaila are Durgā and others; on Sumedha are the Vasus,

1.50.s:
ādityāś ca tathā rudrāḥ kṛtāvāsāstathāśvinau
aśītirdevapuryastu hemakakṣe nagottame //
1.50.d:
आदित्याश् च तथा रुद्राः कृतावासास्तथाश्विनौ
अशीतिर्देवपुर्यस्तु हेमकक्षे नगोत्तमे ॥
1.50.m:
the Ādityas, the Rudras, and the two Aśvins have made their dwelling;
and eighty cities of the gods are on Hemakakṣa, that best of mountains.

1.50.s:
sunīle rakṣasāṃ vāsāḥ pañcakoṭiśatāni ca
pañcakūṭe purāṇyāsan pañcakoṭipramāṇataḥ //
1.50.d:
सुनीले रक्षसां वासाः पञ्चकोटिशतानि च
पञ्चकूटे पुराण्यासन् पञ्चकोटिप्रमाणतः ॥
1.50.m: On Sunīla are the dwellings of the rākṣasas, five hundred crores [in number]; / on Pañcakūṭa were cities to the measure of five crores.

1.50.s:
śataśṛṅge puraśataṃ yakṣāṇāmamitaujasām
tāmrābhe kādraveyāṇāṃ viśākhe tu guhasya vai //
1.50.d:
शतशृङ्गे पुरशतं यक्षाणाममितौजसाम्
ताम्राभे काद्रवेयाणां विशाखे तु गुहस्य वै ॥
1.50.m: On Śataśṛṅga is a hundred cities of the yakṣas of boundless splendour; / on Tāmrābha, of the descendants of Kadru; on Viśākha, indeed, of Guha;

1.50.s:
śvetodare muniśreṣṭhāḥ suparṇasya mahātmanaḥ
piśācake kuberasya harikūṭe harergṛham //
1.50.d:
श्वेतोदरे मुनिश्रेष्ठाः सुपर्णस्य महात्मनः
पिशाचके कुबेरस्य हरिकूटे हरेर्गृहम् ॥
1.50.m: on Śvetodara, O best of sages, of the great-souled Suparṇa; / on Piśācaka, of Kubera; on Harikūṭa is the abode of Hari;

1.50.s:
kumude kiṃnarāvāsas tv añjane cāraṇālayaḥ
kṛṣṇe gandharvanilayaḥ pāṇḍure purasaptakam //
1.50.d:
कुमुदे किंनरावासस् त्व् अञ्जने चारणालयः
कृष्णे गन्धर्वनिलयः पाण्डुरे पुरसप्तकम् ॥
1.50.m: on Kumuda is the dwelling of the kiṃnaras, and on Añjana the abode of the cāraṇas; / on Kṛṣṇa is the residence of the gandharvas; on Pāṇḍura are seven cities,

1.50.s:
vidyādharāṇāṃ viprendrā viśvabhogasamanvitam
sahasraśikhare śaile daityānāmugrakarmaṇām //
1.50.d:
विद्याधराणां विप्रेन्द्रा विश्वभोगसमन्वितम्
सहस्रशिखरे शैले दैत्यानामुग्रकर्मणाम् ॥
1.50.m: O best of brahmins, endowed with all enjoyments, belonging to the vidyādharas; / on the mountain Sahasraśikhara, of the daityas of fierce deeds,

1.50.s:
purāṇāṃ tu sahasrāṇi sapta śakrāriṇāṃ dvijāḥ
mukuṭe pannagāvāsaḥ puṣpaketau munīśvarāḥ //
1.50.d:
पुराणां तु सहस्राणि सप्त शक्रारिणां द्विजाः
मुकुटे पन्नगावासः पुष्पकेतौ मुनीश्वराः ॥
1.50.m: there are seven thousand cities, O twice-born ones, of the enemies of Śakra; / on Mukuṭa is the dwelling of the serpents; on Puṣpaketu, O lords of sages,

1.50.s:
vaivasvatasya somasya vāyornāgādhipasya ca
takṣake caiva śailendre catvāryāyatanāni ca //
1.50.d:
वैवस्वतस्य सोमस्य वायोर्नागाधिपस्य च
तक्षके चैव शैलेन्द्रे चत्वार्यायतनानि च ॥
1.50.m: and on the king of mountains Takṣaka, there are four sanctuaries: / of Vaivasvata, of Soma, of Vāyu, and of the lord of the nāgas;

1.50.s:
brahmendraviṣṇurudrāṇāṃ guhasya ca mahātmanaḥ
kuberasya ca somasya tathānyeṣāṃ mahātmanām //
1.50.d:
ब्रह्मेन्द्रविष्णुरुद्राणां गुहस्य च महात्मनः
कुबेरस्य च सोमस्य तथान्येषां महात्मनाम् ॥
1.50.m: and of Brahmā, Indra, Viṣṇu, and the Rudras, and of the great-souled Guha, / and of Kubera, and of Soma, and likewise of other great-souled ones.

1.50.s:
santyāyatanamukhyāni maryādāparvateṣvapi
śrīkaṇṭhādriguhāvāsī sarvāvāsaḥ sahomayā //
1.50.d:
सन्त्यायतनमुख्यानि मर्यादापर्वतेष्वपि
श्रीकण्ठाद्रिगुहावासी सर्वावासः सहोमया ॥
1.50.m: There are prominent sanctuaries also on the boundary mountains. / Śrīkaṇṭha dwells in the caves of the mountains, dwelling everywhere together with Umā.

1.50.s:
śrīkaṇṭhasyādhipatyaṃ vai sarvadeveśvarasya ca
aṇḍasyāsya pravṛttistu śrīkaṇṭhena na saṃśayaḥ //
1.50.d:
श्रीकण्ठस्याधिपत्यं वै सर्वदेवेश्वरस्य च
अण्डस्यास्य प्रवृत्तिस्तु श्रीकण्ठेन न संशयः ॥
1.50.m: The sovereign lordship belongs indeed to Śrīkaṇṭha, the lord of all the gods; / and the functioning of this cosmic egg proceeds from Śrīkaṇṭha, no doubt.

1.50.s:
ananteśādayastvevaṃ pratyekaṃ cāṇḍapālakāḥ
cakravartina ityuktās tato vidyeśvarāstviha //
1.50.d:
अनन्तेशादयस्त्वेवं प्रत्येकं चाण्डपालकाः
चक्रवर्तिन इत्युक्तास् ततो विद्येश्वरास्त्विह ॥
1.50.m: Ananteśa and others are thus each guardians of the cosmic egg, / said to be emperors, and then here the Vidyeśvaras.

1.50.s:
śrīkaṇṭhādhiṣṭhitānyatra sthānāni ca samāsataḥ
maryādāparvateṣvadya śṛṇvantu pravadāmy aham //
1.50.d:
श्रीकण्ठाधिष्ठितान्यत्र स्थानानि च समासतः
मर्यादापर्वतेष्वद्य शृण्वन्तु प्रवदाम्य् अहम् ॥
1.50.m: The abodes here presided over by Śrīkaṇṭha in brief / on the boundary mountains, listen, I will speak of today.

1.50.s:
śrīkaṇṭhādhiṣṭhitaṃ viśvaṃ carācaramidaṃ jagat
kālāgniśivaparyantaṃ kathaṃ vakṣye savistaram //
1.50.d:
श्रीकण्ठाधिष्ठितं विश्वं चराचरमिदं जगत्
कालाग्निशिवपर्यन्तं कथं वक्ष्ये सविस्तरम् ॥
1.50.m: Presided over by Śrīkaṇṭha is this entire moving and unmoving world; / up to Kālāgni-Śiva, how could I describe it in full detail?

1.51.s:
sūta uvāca
devakūṭe girau madhye mahākūṭe suśobhane
hemavaiḍūryamāṇikyanīlagomedakāntibhiḥ //
1.51.d:
सूत उवाच
देवकूटे गिरौ मध्ये महाकूटे सुशोभने
हेमवैडूर्यमाणिक्यनीलगोमेदकान्तिभिः ॥
1.51.m: Sūta said: / On Mount Devakūṭa, in the centre, on the Mahākūṭa, exceedingly splendid, / with the lustres of gold, lapis lazuli, ruby, sapphire, and agate,

1.51.s:
tathānyairmaṇimukhyaiś ca nirmite nirmale śubhe
śākhāśatasahasrāḍhye sarvadrumavibhūṣite //
1.51.d:
तथान्यैर्मणिमुख्यैश् च निर्मिते निर्मले शुभे
शाखाशतसहस्राढ्ये सर्वद्रुमविभूषिते ॥
1.51.m: and made of other choice jewels, spotless and auspicious, / rich in hundreds of thousands of branches, adorned with all [kinds of] trees,

1.51.s:
campakāśokapuṃnāgavakulāsanamaṇḍite
pārijātakasampūrṇe nānāpakṣigaṇānvite //
1.51.d:
चम्पकाशोकपुंनागवकुलासनमण्डिते
पारिजातकसम्पूर्णे नानापक्षिगणान्विते ॥
1.51.m: graced with campaka, aśoka, puṃnāga, vakula, and asana, / filled with pārijātaka, accompanied by various flocks of birds,

1.51.s:
naikadhātuśataiścitre vicitrakusumākule
nitambapuṣpasālamben-aikasattvagaṇānvite //
1.51.d:
नैकधातुशतैश्चित्रे विचित्रकुसुमाकुले
नितम्बपुष्पसालम्बेन्-ऐकसत्त्वगणान्विते ॥
1.51.m: variegated with hundreds of manifold minerals, crowded with wonderful flowers, / with flowers hanging from its slopes, accompanied by numerous herds of creatures,

1.51.s:
vimalasvādupānīyen-aikaprasravaṇairyute
nirjharaiḥ kusumākīrṇair anekaiś ca vibhūṣite //
1.51.d:
विमलस्वादुपानीयेन्-ऐकप्रस्रवणैर्युते
निर्झरैः कुसुमाकीर्णैर् अनेकैश् च विभूषिते ॥
1.51.m: provided with clear, sweet water and many streams, / and adorned with many cascading waterfalls strewn with flowers,

1.51.s:
puṣpoḍupavahābhiś ca sravantībhir alaṃkṛte
snigdhavarṇaṃ mahāmūlam anekaskandhapādapam //
1.51.d:
पुष्पोडुपवहाभिश् च स्रवन्तीभिर् अलंकृते
स्निग्धवर्णं महामूलम् अनेकस्कन्धपादपम् ॥
1.51.m: and decorated with rivers that carry rafts of flowers, / [there is a forest] of glossy colour, having great roots and trees with numerous trunks,

1.51.s:
ramyaṃ hyaviralacchāyaṃ daśayojanamaṇḍalam
tatra bhūtavanaṃ nāma nānābhūtagaṇālayam //
1.51.d:
रम्यं ह्यविरलच्छायं दशयोजनमण्डलम्
तत्र भूतवनं नाम नानाभूतगणालयम् ॥
1.51.m: delightful, indeed, with dense shade, ten yojanas in circumference; / there is [a forest] named Bhūtavana, the abode of various multitudes of spirits.

1.51.s:
mahādevasya devasya śaṅkarasya mahātmanaḥ
dīptamāyatanaṃ tatra mahāmaṇivibhūṣitam //
1.51.d:
महादेवस्य देवस्य शङ्करस्य महात्मनः
दीप्तमायतनं तत्र महामणिविभूषितम् ॥
1.51.m: There is a radiant sanctuary of the god Mahādeva, / the great-souled Śaṅkara, adorned with magnificent gems,

1.51.s:
hemaprākārasaṃyuktaṃ maṇitoraṇamaṇḍitam
sphāṭikaiś ca vicitraiś ca gopuraiś ca samanvitam //
1.51.d:
हेमप्राकारसंयुक्तं मणितोरणमण्डितम्
स्फाटिकैश् च विचित्रैश् च गोपुरैश् च समन्वितम् ॥
1.51.m: endowed with a golden rampart, decorated with jewelled archways, / and accompanied by varied gateways made of crystal,

1.51.s:
siṃhāsanairmaṇimayaiḥ śubhāstaraṇasaṃyutaiḥ
kṣitāvitastataḥ samyak śarveṇādhiṣṭhitaiḥ śubhaiḥ //
1.51.d:
सिंहासनैर्मणिमयैः शुभास्तरणसंयुतैः
क्षितावितस्ततः सम्यक् शर्वेणाधिष्ठितैः शुभैः ॥
1.51.m: with jewelled thrones provided with auspicious coverings / placed firmly here and there on the ground, occupied by the auspicious Śarva,

1.51.s:
amlānamālānicitair nānāvarṇair gṛhottamaiḥ
maṇḍapaiḥ suvicitrais tu sphāṭikastambhasaṃyutaiḥ //
1.51.d:
अम्लानमालानिचितैर् नानावर्णैर् गृहोत्तमैः
मण्डपैः सुविचित्रैस् तु स्फाटिकस्तम्भसंयुतैः ॥
1.51.m: with excellent halls of various colours heaped with unfading garlands, / and with most wonderful pavilions accompanied by pillars of crystal,

1.51.s:
saṃyutaṃ sarvabhūtendrair brahmendropendrapūjitaiḥ
varāhagajasiṃharkṣaśārdūlakarabhānanaiḥ //
1.51.d:
संयुतं सर्वभूतेन्द्रैर् ब्रह्मेन्द्रोपेन्द्रपूजितैः
वराहगजसिंहर्क्षशार्दूलकरभाननैः ॥
1.51.m: thronged by all the lords of spirits worshipped by Brahmā, Indra, and Upendra, / with faces of boars, elephants, lions, bears, tigers, and young camels,

1.51.s:
gṛdhrolūkamukhaiścānyair mṛgoṣṭrājamukhairapi
pramathairvividhaiḥ sthūlair girikūṭopamaiḥ śubhaiḥ //
1.51.d:
गृध्रोलूकमुखैश्चान्यैर् मृगोष्ट्राजमुखैरपि
प्रमथैर्विविधैः स्थूलैर् गिरिकूटोपमैः शुभैः ॥
1.51.m: and others with faces of vultures and owls, and faces of deer, camels, and goats, / with various thick pramathas resembling mountain peaks, auspicious,

1.51.s:
karālairharikeśaiś ca romaśaiś ca mahābhujaiḥ
nānāvarṇākṛtidharair nānāsaṃsthānasaṃsthitaiḥ //
1.51.d:
करालैर्हरिकेशैश् च रोमशैश् च महाभुजैः
नानावर्णाकृतिधरैर् नानासंस्थानसंस्थितैः ॥
1.51.m: dreadful, yellow-haired, hairy, and mighty-armed, / bearing diverse colours and forms, situated in various postures,

1.51.s:
dīptāsyair dīptacaritair nandīśvaramukhaiḥ śubhaiḥ
brahmendraviṣṇusaṃkāśair aṇimādiguṇānvitaiḥ //
1.51.d:
दीप्तास्यैर् दीप्तचरितैर् नन्दीश्वरमुखैः शुभैः
ब्रह्मेन्द्रविष्णुसंकाशैर् अणिमादिगुणान्वितैः ॥
1.51.m: with blazing mouths, of glowing conduct, auspicious, headed by Nandīśvara, / resembling Brahmā, Indra, and Viṣṇu, endowed with the supernatural powers of aṇimā and the rest,

1.51.s:
aśūnyamamarairnityaṃ mahāpariṣadais tathā
tatra bhūtapaterdevāḥ pūjāṃ nityaṃ prayuñjate //
1.51.d:
अशून्यममरैर्नित्यं महापरिषदैस् तथा
तत्र भूतपतेर्देवाः पूजां नित्यं प्रयुञ्जते ॥
1.51.m: never empty of the immortals and of the great assembly. / There the gods continually perform worship to the lord of spirits,

1.51.s:
jharjharaiḥ śaṅkhapaṭahair bherīḍiṇḍimagomukhaiḥ
lalitāvasitodgītair vṛttavalgitagarjitaiḥ //
1.51.d:
झर्झरैः शङ्खपटहैर् भेरीडिण्डिमगोमुखैः
ललितावसितोद्गीतैर् वृत्तवल्गितगर्जितैः ॥
1.51.m: with jharjharas, conches, paṭahas, bherīs, ḍiṇḍimas, and gomukhas, / with graceful, melodious singing, and with dances, leaps, and roaring cries.

1.51.s:
pūjito vai mahādevaḥ pramathaiḥ pramatheśvaraḥ
siddharṣidevagandharvair brahmaṇā ca mahātmanā //
1.51.d:
पूजितो वै महादेवः प्रमथैः प्रमथेश्वरः
सिद्धर्षिदेवगन्धर्वैर् ब्रह्मणा च महात्मना ॥
1.51.m: Indeed, Mahādeva, the lord of pramathas, is worshipped by the pramathas, / by the siddhas, sages, gods, and gandharvas, and by the great-souled Brahmā,

1.51.s:
upendrapramukhaiścānyaiḥ pūjitastatra śaṃkaraḥ
vibhaktacāruśikharaṃ yatra tacchaṅkhavarcasam //
1.51.d:
उपेन्द्रप्रमुखैश्चान्यैः पूजितस्तत्र शंकरः
विभक्तचारुशिखरं यत्र तच्छङ्खवर्चसम् ॥
1.51.m: and Śaṅkara is worshipped there by others headed by Upendra. / Where that conch-bright [peak] has beautiful separated ridges,

1.51.s:
kailāso yakṣarājasya kuberasya mahātmanaḥ
nivāsaḥ koṭiyakṣāṇāṃ tathānyeṣāṃ mahātmanām //
1.51.d:
कैलासो यक्षराजस्य कुबेरस्य महात्मनः
निवासः कोटियक्षाणां तथान्येषां महात्मनाम् ॥
1.51.m: is Kailāsa, of the great-souled Kubera, king of the yakṣas, / the dwelling of crores of yakṣas and of other great-souled ones.

1.51.s:
tatrāpi devadevasya bhavasyāyatanaṃ mahat
tasminnāyatane somaḥ sadāste sagaṇo haraḥ //
1.51.d:
तत्रापि देवदेवस्य भवस्यायतनं महत्
तस्मिन्नायतने सोमः सदास्ते सगणो हरः ॥
1.51.m: There too is the great sanctuary of the god of gods, Bhava; / in that sanctuary, Hara, along with Soma and his gaṇas, ever resides.

1.51.s:
yatra mandākinī nāma nalinī vipulodakā
suvarṇamaṇisopānā kuberaśikhare śubhe //
1.51.d:
यत्र मन्दाकिनी नाम नलिनी विपुलोदका
सुवर्णमणिसोपाना कुबेरशिखरे शुभे ॥
1.51.m: Where the lotus-lake named Mandākinī of abundant waters has / stairs of gold and jewels, on the auspicious peak of Kubera,

1.51.s:
jāṃbūnadamayaiḥ padmair gandhasparśaguṇānvitaiḥ
nīlavaiḍūryapatraiś ca gandhopetairmahotpalaiḥ //
1.51.d:
जांबूनदमयैः पद्मैर् गन्धस्पर्शगुणान्वितैः
नीलवैडूर्यपत्रैश् च गन्धोपेतैर्महोत्पलैः ॥
1.51.m: adorned with golden lotuses endowed with qualities of fragrance and touch, / with leaves of blue lapis lazuli and great blue water lilies possessed of scent,

1.51.s:
tathā kumudaṣaṇḍaiś ca mahāpadmair alaṃkṛtā
yakṣagandharvanārībhir apsarobhiś ca sevitā //
1.51.d:
तथा कुमुदषण्डैश् च महापद्मैर् अलंकृता
यक्षगन्धर्वनारीभिर् अप्सरोभिश् च सेविता ॥
1.51.m: as well as with clusters of night-lotuses and great lotuses, / frequented by the women of the yakṣas and gandharvas and by apsarases,

1.51.s:
devadānavagandharvair yakṣarākṣasakinnaraiḥ
upaspṛṣṭajalā puṇyā nadī mandākinī śubhā //
1.51.d:
देवदानवगन्धर्वैर् यक्षराक्षसकिन्नरैः
उपस्पृष्टजला पुण्या नदी मन्दाकिनी शुभा ॥
1.51.m: its waters bathed in by gods, dānavas, gandharvas, / yakṣas, rākṣasas, and kinnaras—the auspicious, holy river Mandākinī.

1.51.s:
tasyāścottarapārśve tu bhavasyāyatanaṃ śubham
vaiḍūryamaṇisampannaṃ tatrāste śaṅkaro 'vyayaḥ //
1.51.d:
तस्याश्चोत्तरपार्श्वे तु भवस्यायतनं शुभम्
वैडूर्यमणिसम्पन्नं तत्रास्ते शङ्करो ऽव्ययः ॥
1.51.m: And on its northern flank is the auspicious sanctuary of Bhava, / endowed with lapis lazuli and jewels; there the imperishable Śaṅkara resides.

1.51.s:
dvijāḥ kanakanandāyās tīre vai prāci dakṣiṇe
vanaṃ dvijasahasrāḍhyaṃ mṛgapakṣisamākulam //
1.51.d:
द्विजाः कनकनन्दायास् तीरे वै प्राचि दक्षिणे
वनं द्विजसहस्राढ्यं मृगपक्षिसमाकुलम् ॥
1.51.m: O twice-born ones, on the south-eastern bank of the Kanakanandā / is a forest rich in thousands of birds, crowded with beasts and birds;

1.51.s:
tatrāpi sagaṇaḥ sāmbaḥ krīḍate 'drisame gṛhe
nandāyāḥ paścime tīre kiṃcid vai dakṣiṇāśrite //
1.51.d:
तत्रापि सगणः साम्बः क्रीडते ऽद्रिसमे गृहे
नन्दायाः पश्चिमे तीरे किंचिद् वै दक्षिणाश्रिते ॥
1.51.m: there too, accompanied by his gaṇas and with Ambā, he plays in an abode resembling a mountain. / On the western bank of the Nandā, leaning somewhat towards the south,

1.51.s:
puraṃ rudrapurī nāma nānāprāsādasaṃkulam
tatrāpi śatadhā kṛtvā hy ātmānaṃ cāmbayā saha //
1.51.d:
पुरं रुद्रपुरी नाम नानाप्रासादसंकुलम्
तत्रापि शतधा कृत्वा ह्य् आत्मानं चाम्बया सह ॥
1.51.m: is a city named Rudrapurī, filled with various mansions; / there too, having made himself into a hundred forms, together with the Mother,

1.51.s:
krīḍate sagaṇaḥ sāmbas tacchivālayam ucyate
evaṃ śatasahasrāṇi śarvasyāyatanāni tu //
1.51.d:
क्रीडते सगणः साम्बस् तच्छिवालयम् उच्यते
एवं शतसहस्राणि शर्वस्यायतनानि तु ॥
1.51.m: accompanied by his gaṇas and with Ambā, he plays; that is called the abode of Śiva. / Thus there are hundreds of thousands of sanctuaries of Śarva,

1.51.s:
pratidvīpe muniśreṣṭhāḥ parvateṣu vaneṣu ca
nadīnadataṭākānāṃ tīreṣvarṇavasaṃdhiṣu //
1.51.d:
प्रतिद्वीपे मुनिश्रेष्ठाः पर्वतेषु वनेषु च
नदीनदतटाकानां तीरेष्वर्णवसंधिषु ॥
1.51.m: O best of sages, on every continent, in mountains and in forests, / on the banks of rivers, streams, and lakes, and at the junctions of the oceans.

1.52.s:
sūta uvāca
nadyaś ca bahavaḥ proktāḥ sadā bahujalāḥ śubhāḥ
sarovarebhyaḥ sambhūtās tv asaṃkhyātā dvijottamāḥ //
1.52.d:
सूत उवाच
नद्यश् च बहवः प्रोक्ताः सदा बहुजलाः शुभाः
सरोवरेभ्यः सम्भूतास् त्व् असंख्याता द्विजोत्तमाः ॥
1.52.m: Sūta said: / Many rivers are proclaimed, always with abundant waters and auspicious; / they have arisen from lakes, innumerable, O best of the twice-born,

1.52.s:
prāṅmukhā dakṣiṇāsyāstu cottaraprabhavāḥ śubhāḥ
paścimāgrāḥ pavitrāś ca prativarṣaṃ prakīrtitāḥ //
1.52.d:
प्राङ्मुखा दक्षिणास्यास्तु चोत्तरप्रभवाः शुभाः
पश्चिमाग्राः पवित्राश् च प्रतिवर्षं प्रकीर्तिताः ॥
1.52.m: flowing eastward, facing southward, and originating in the north, auspicious, / flowing westward and purifying; they are proclaimed for each realm.

1.52.s:
ākāśāṃbhonidhir yo 'sau soma ityabhidhīyate
ādhāraḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ devānāmamṛtākaraḥ //
1.52.d:
आकाशांभोनिधिर् यो ऽसौ सोम इत्यभिधीयते
आधारः सर्वभूतानां देवानाममृताकरः ॥
1.52.m: That reservoir of celestial waters which is called Soma, / the support of all beings, a mine of nectar for the gods—

1.52.s:
asmātpravṛttā puṇyodā nadī tvākāśagāminī
saptamenānilapathā pravṛttā cāmṛtodakā //
1.52.d:
अस्मात्प्रवृत्ता पुण्योदा नदी त्वाकाशगामिनी
सप्तमेनानिलपथा प्रवृत्ता चामृतोदका ॥
1.52.m: from this the sky-faring river of holy waters issued forth; / along the seventh path of the wind it issued, with waters of nectar.

1.52.s:
sā jyotīṃṣyanuvartantī jyotirgaṇaniṣevitā
tārākoṭisahasrāṇāṃ nabhasaś ca samāyutā //
1.52.d:
सा ज्योतींष्यनुवर्तन्ती ज्योतिर्गणनिषेविता
ताराकोटिसहस्राणां नभसश् च समायुता ॥
1.52.m: Following the celestial luminaries, frequented by hosts of stars, / and united with thousands of crores of stars of the sky,

1.52.s:
parivartatyaharaho yathā somastathaiva sā
catvāryaśītiś ca tathā sahasrāṇāṃ samucchritaḥ //
1.52.d:
परिवर्तत्यहरहो यथा सोमस्तथैव सा
चत्वार्यशीतिश् च तथा सहस्राणां समुच्छ्रितः ॥
1.52.m: she turns day by day just as the Moon does. / And eighty-four thousand [yojanas] high

1.52.s:
yojanānāṃ mahāmeruḥ śrīkaṇṭhākrīḍakomalaḥ
tatrāsīno yataḥ śarvaḥ sāmbaḥ saha gaṇeśvaraiḥ //
1.52.d:
योजनानां महामेरुः श्रीकण्ठाक्रीडकोमलः
तत्रासीनो यतः शर्वः साम्बः सह गणेश्वरैः ॥
1.52.m: in yojanas is Great Meru, tender with the pleasure-grounds of Śrīkaṇṭha; / because Śarva sits there with Ambā and the lords of the gaṇas,

1.52.s:
krīḍate suciraṃ kālaṃ tasmātpuṇyajalā śivā
giriṃ meruṃ nadī puṇyā sā prayāti pradakṣiṇam //
1.52.d:
क्रीडते सुचिरं कालं तस्मात्पुण्यजला शिवा
गिरिं मेरुं नदी पुण्या सा प्रयाति प्रदक्षिणम् ॥
1.52.m: sporting for a very long time, therefore that auspicious river of holy waters / goes clockwise around Mount Meru.

1.52.s:
vibhajyamānasalilā sā javenānilena ca
merorantarakūṭeṣu nipapāta caturṣvapi //
1.52.d:
विभज्यमानसलिला सा जवेनानिलेन च
मेरोरन्तरकूटेषु निपपात चतुर्ष्वपि ॥
1.52.m: With her waters divided by her speed and by the wind, / she fell upon all four intermediate peaks of Meru.

1.52.s:
samantātsamatikramya sarvādrīnpravibhāgaśaḥ
niyogāddevadevasya praviṣṭā sā mahārṇavam //
1.52.d:
समन्तात्समतिक्रम्य सर्वाद्रीन्प्रविभागशः
नियोगाद्देवदेवस्य प्रविष्टा सा महार्णवम् ॥
1.52.m: Traversing completely around all the mountains according to their divisions, / she entered the great ocean by command of the God of gods.

1.52.s:
asyā vinirgatā nadyaḥ śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ
sarvadvīpādrivarṣeṣu bahavaḥ parikīrtitāḥ //
1.52.d:
अस्या विनिर्गता नद्यः शतशो ऽथ सहस्रशः
सर्वद्वीपाद्रिवर्षेषु बहवः परिकीर्तिताः ॥
1.52.m: Emerging from her, rivers in their hundreds and thousands / are proclaimed throughout all the continents, mountains, and regions.

1.52.s:
kṣudranadyastvasaṃkhyātā gaṅgā yadgāṅgatāmbarāt
ketumāle narāḥ kālāḥ sarve panasabhojanāḥ //
1.52.d:
क्षुद्रनद्यस्त्वसंख्याता गङ्गा यद्गाङ्गताम्बरात्
केतुमाले नराः कालाः सर्वे पनसभोजनाः ॥
1.52.m: Countless are the lesser rivers, since Gaṅgā came from the sky. / In Ketumāla, men are dark-complexioned, and all subsist on jackfruit.

1.52.s:
striyaścotpalavarṇābhā jīvitaṃ cāyutaṃ smṛtam
bhadrāśve śuklavarṇāś ca striyaścandrāṃśusaṃnibhāḥ //
1.52.d:
स्त्रियश्चोत्पलवर्णाभा जीवितं चायुतं स्मृतम्
भद्राश्वे शुक्लवर्णाश् च स्त्रियश्चन्द्रांशुसंनिभाः ॥
1.52.m: The women have the radiance of blue lotus petals, and their lifespan is remembered as ten thousand [years]. / In Bhadrāśva, men are white-complexioned, and the women resemble rays of the moon.

1.52.s:
kālāmrabhojanāḥ sarve nirātaṅkā ratipriyāḥ
daśavarṣasahasrāṇi jīvanti śivabhāvitāḥ //
1.52.d:
कालाम्रभोजनाः सर्वे निरातङ्का रतिप्रियाः
दशवर्षसहस्राणि जीवन्ति शिवभाविताः ॥
1.52.m: All eat dark mangoes, free from sickness, fond of amorous delight; / they live for ten thousand years, devoted to Śiva.

1.52.s:
hiraṇmayā ivātyartham īśvarārpitacetasaḥ
tathā ramaṇake jīvā nyagrodhaphalabhojanāḥ //
1.52.d:
हिरण्मया इवात्यर्थम् ईश्वरार्पितचेतसः
तथा रमणके जीवा न्यग्रोधफलभोजनाः ॥
1.52.m: They are exceedingly radiant like gold, their minds dedicated to the Lord. / Likewise in Ramaṇaka, living beings subsist on banyan fruits;

1.52.s:
daśavarṣasahasrāṇi śatāni daśapañca ca
jīvanti śuklāste sarve śivadhyānaparāyaṇāḥ //
1.52.d:
दशवर्षसहस्राणि शतानि दशपञ्च च
जीवन्ति शुक्लास्ते सर्वे शिवध्यानपरायणाः ॥
1.52.m: they live for ten thousand and fifteen hundred years, / all of them fair, dedicated to meditation on Śiva.

1.52.s:
hairaṇmayā mahābhāgā hiraṇmayavanāśrayāḥ
ekādaśa sahasrāṇi śatāni daśapañca ca //
1.52.d:
हैरण्मया महाभागा हिरण्मयवनाश्रयाः
एकादश सहस्राणि शतानि दशपञ्च च ॥
1.52.m: The fortunate inhabitants of Hiraṇmaya resort to the golden forest; / for eleven thousand and fifteen hundred

1.52.s:
varṣāṇāṃ tatra jīvanti aśvatthāśanajīvanāḥ
hairaṇmayā ivātyartham īśvarārpitamānasāḥ //
1.52.d:
वर्षाणां तत्र जीवन्ति अश्वत्थाशनजीवनाः
हैरण्मया इवात्यर्थम् ईश्वरार्पितमानसाः ॥
1.52.m: years they live there, sustaining life by eating sacred-fig fruits, / exceedingly like gold, their minds dedicated to the Lord.

1.52.s:
kuruvarṣe tu kuravaḥ svargalokāt paricyutāḥ
sarve maithunajātāś ca kṣīriṇaḥ kṣīrabhojanāḥ //
1.52.d:
कुरुवर्षे तु कुरवः स्वर्गलोकात् परिच्युताः
सर्वे मैथुनजाताश् च क्षीरिणः क्षीरभोजनाः ॥
1.52.m: In the region of Kuru, however, the Kurus are fallen from the world of heaven; / all are born of sexual union, possessed of milch trees, subsisting on milky sap.

1.52.s:
anyonyamanuraktāś ca cakravākasadharmiṇaḥ
anāmayā hyaśokāś ca nityaṃ sukhaniṣeviṇaḥ //
1.52.d:
अन्योन्यमनुरक्ताश् च चक्रवाकसधर्मिणः
अनामया ह्यशोकाश् च नित्यं सुखनिषेविणः ॥
1.52.m: They are attached to one another, behaving like cakravāka birds, / free from disease and grief, constantly enjoying pleasure.

1.52.s:
trayodaśasahasrāṇi śatāni daśapañca ca
jīvanti te mahāvīryā na cānyastrīniṣeviṇaḥ //
1.52.d:
त्रयोदशसहस्राणि शतानि दशपञ्च च
जीवन्ति ते महावीर्या न चान्यस्त्रीनिषेविणः ॥
1.52.m: For thirteen thousand and fifteen hundred [years] / they live, endowed with great prowess, never resorting to other women.

1.52.s:
sahaiva maraṇaṃ teṣāṃ kurūṇāṃ svargavāsinām
hṛṣṭānāṃ supravṛddhānāṃ sarvānnāmṛtabhojinām //
1.52.d:
सहैव मरणं तेषां कुरूणां स्वर्गवासिनाम्
हृष्टानां सुप्रवृद्धानां सर्वान्नामृतभोजिनाम् ॥
1.52.m: Death comes together for those Kurus who dwell like heavenly beings, / joyful, fully grown, eating divine nectar that yields all foods,

1.52.s:
sadā tu candrakāntānāṃ sadā yauvanaśālinām
śyāmāṅgānāṃ sadā sarvabhūṣaṇāspadadehinām //
1.52.d:
सदा तु चन्द्रकान्तानां सदा यौवनशालिनाम्
श्यामाङ्गानां सदा सर्वभूषणास्पददेहिनाम् ॥
1.52.m: ever moon-lovely, ever endowed with youth, / their limbs dark-hued, their bodies ever an abode for all ornaments.

1.52.s:
jaṃbūdvīpe tu tatrāpi kuruvarṣaṃ suśobhanam
tatra candraprabhaṃ śambhor vimānaṃ candramaulinaḥ //
1.52.d:
जंबूद्वीपे तु तत्रापि कुरुवर्षं सुशोभनम्
तत्र चन्द्रप्रभं शम्भोर् विमानं चन्द्रमौलिनः ॥
1.52.m: In Jambūdvīpa, even there, the Kuru region is exceedingly radiant; / there is the moon-bright celestial chariot of Śambhu, whose crest is the moon.

1.52.s:
varṣe tu bhārate martyāḥ puṇyāḥ karmavaśāyuṣaḥ
śatāyuṣaḥ samākhyātā nānāvarṇālpadehinaḥ //
1.52.d:
वर्षे तु भारते मर्त्याः पुण्याः कर्मवशायुषः
शतायुषः समाख्याता नानावर्णाल्पदेहिनः ॥
1.52.m: In the region of Bhārata, however, mortals are righteous, their lifespans determined by action; / they are declared to live a hundred years, of various castes and small bodies,

1.52.s:
nānādevārcane yuktā nānākarmaphalāśinaḥ
nānājñānārthasampannā durbalāścālpabhoginaḥ //
1.52.d:
नानादेवार्चने युक्ता नानाकर्मफलाशिनः
नानाज्ञानार्थसम्पन्ना दुर्बलाश्चाल्पभोगिनः ॥
1.52.m: intent on worshipping various deities, tasting the fruits of diverse actions, / endowed with various forms of knowledge and wealth, weak, and of little enjoyment.

1.52.s:
indradvīpe tathā kecit tathaiva ca kaseruke
tāmradvīpaṃ gatāḥ kecit keciddeśaṃ gabhastimat //
1.52.d:
इन्द्रद्वीपे तथा केचित् तथैव च कसेरुके
ताम्रद्वीपं गताः केचित् केचिद्देशं गभस्तिमत् ॥
1.52.m: Some dwell in Indradvīpa, and likewise in Kaseruka; / some have gone to Tāmradvīpa, and some to the region of Gabhastimat;

1.52.s:
nāgadvīpaṃ tathā saumyaṃ gāndharvaṃ vāruṇaṃ gatāḥ
kecinmlecchāḥ pulindāś ca nānājātisamudbhavāḥ //
1.52.d:
नागद्वीपं तथा सौम्यं गान्धर्वं वारुणं गताः
केचिन्म्लेच्छाः पुलिन्दाश् च नानाजातिसमुद्भवाः ॥
1.52.m: some have gone to Nāgadvīpa, Saumya, Gāndharva, and Vāruṇa; / some are Mlecchas and Pulindas, born of various origins.

1.52.s:
pūrve kirātāstasyānte paścime yavanāḥ smṛtāḥ
brāhmaṇāḥ kṣatriyā vaiśyā madhye śūdrāś ca sarvaśaḥ //
1.52.d:
पूर्वे किरातास्तस्यान्ते पश्चिमे यवनाः स्मृताः
ब्राह्मणाः क्षत्रिया वैश्या मध्ये शूद्राश् च सर्वशः ॥
1.52.m: In the east are the Kirātas; at its western boundary the Yavanas are recorded; / in the middle are Brāhmaṇas, Kṣatriyas, Vaiśyas, and Śūdras everywhere,

1.52.s:
ijyāyuddhavaṇijyābhir vartayanto vyavasthitāḥ
teṣāṃ saṃvyavahāro 'yaṃ vartate 'tra parasparam //
1.52.d:
इज्यायुद्धवणिज्याभिर् वर्तयन्तो व्यवस्थिताः
तेषां संव्यवहारो ऽयं वर्तते ऽत्र परस्परम् ॥
1.52.m: settled and sustaining themselves through sacrifice, battle, and trade; / their mutual intercourse is conducted here,

1.52.s:
dharmārthakāmasaṃyukto varṇānāṃ tu svakarmasu
saṃkalpaścābhimānaś ca āśramāṇāṃ yathāvidhi //
1.52.d:
धर्मार्थकामसंयुक्तो वर्णानां तु स्वकर्मसु
संकल्पश्चाभिमानश् च आश्रमाणां यथाविधि ॥
1.52.m: joined with dharma, wealth, and pleasure according to the proper duties of the castes, / and the resolves and proper pride of the stages of life according to rule.

1.52.s:
iha svargāpavargārthaṃ pravṛttiryatra mānuṣī
teṣāṃ ca yugakarmāṇi nānyatra munipuṅgavāḥ //
1.52.d:
इह स्वर्गापवर्गार्थं प्रवृत्तिर्यत्र मानुषी
तेषां च युगकर्माणि नान्यत्र मुनिपुङ्गवाः ॥
1.52.m: Here human activity takes place for the sake of heaven and liberation; / and for them are the actions of the yugas, nowhere else, O best of sages.

1.52.s:
daśavarṣasahasrāṇi sthitiḥ kiṃpuruṣe nṛṇām
suvarṇavarṇāś ca narāḥ striyaścāpsarasopamāḥ //
1.52.d:
दशवर्षसहस्राणि स्थितिः किंपुरुषे नृणाम्
सुवर्णवर्णाश् च नराः स्त्रियश्चाप्सरसोपमाः ॥
1.52.m: The lifespan of men in Kiṃpuruṣa is ten thousand years; / the men are gold-complexioned, and the women resemble Apsarases.

1.52.s:
anāmayā hyaśokāś ca sarve te śivabhāvitāḥ
śuddhasattvāś ca hemābhāḥ sadārāḥ plakṣabhojanāḥ //
1.52.d:
अनामया ह्यशोकाश् च सर्वे ते शिवभाविताः
शुद्धसत्त्वाश् च हेमाभाः सदाराः प्लक्षभोजनाः ॥
1.52.m: Free from disease and grief, all of them are devoted to Śiva, / of pure sattva, shining like gold, with their wives, subsisting on wave-leafed fig fruits.

1.52.s:
mahārajatasaṃkāśā harivarṣe 'pi mānavāḥ
devalokāccyutāḥ sarve devākārāś ca sarvaśaḥ //
1.52.d:
महारजतसंकाशा हरिवर्षे ऽपि मानवाः
देवलोकाच्च्युताः सर्वे देवाकाराश् च सर्वशः ॥
1.52.m: Resembling refined gold are the men in Harivarṣa also, / all fallen from the world of gods, divine in form in every way.

1.52.s:
haraṃ yajanti sarveśaṃ pibantīkṣurasaṃ śubham
na jarā bādhate tena na ca jīryanti te narāḥ //
1.52.d:
हरं यजन्ति सर्वेशं पिबन्तीक्षुरसं शुभम्
न जरा बाधते तेन न च जीर्यन्ति ते नराः ॥
1.52.m: They worship Hara, Lord of all, and drink auspicious sugarcane juice; / because of that, old age does not afflict them, nor do those men decay.

1.52.s:
daśavarṣasahasrāṇi tatra jīvanti mānavāḥ
madhyamaṃ yanmayā proktaṃ nāmnā varṣamilāvṛtam //
1.52.d:
दशवर्षसहस्राणि तत्र जीवन्ति मानवाः
मध्यमं यन्मया प्रोक्तं नाम्ना वर्षमिलावृतम् ॥
1.52.m: Men live there for ten thousand years. / That central region which I have mentioned, Ilāvṛta by name—

1.52.s:
na tatra sūryastapati na te jīryanti mānavāḥ
candrasūryau na nakṣatraṃ na prakāśam ilāvṛte //
1.52.d:
न तत्र सूर्यस्तपति न ते जीर्यन्ति मानवाः
चन्द्रसूर्यौ न नक्षत्रं न प्रकाशम् इलावृते ॥
1.52.m: there the sun does not burn, nor do men decay; / neither moon, nor sun, nor constellation shines in Ilāvṛta.

1.52.s:
padmaprabhāḥ padmamukhāḥ padmapattranibhekṣaṇāḥ
padmapattrasugandhāś ca jāyante bhavabhāvitāḥ //
1.52.d:
पद्मप्रभाः पद्ममुखाः पद्मपत्त्रनिभेक्षणाः
पद्मपत्त्रसुगन्धाश् च जायन्ते भवभाविताः ॥
1.52.m: Possessing the radiance of lotuses, lotus-faced, with eyes like lotus petals, / and fragrant as lotus petals, they are born, devoted to Bhava.

1.52.s:
jambūphalarasāhārā aniṣpandāḥ sugandhinaḥ
devalokāgatāstatra jāyante hyajarāmarāḥ //
1.52.d:
जम्बूफलरसाहारा अनिष्पन्दाः सुगन्धिनः
देवलोकागतास्तत्र जायन्ते ह्यजरामराः ॥
1.52.m: Feeding on the juice of the jambu fruit, motionless, fragrant, / coming from the world of the gods, they are indeed born there ageless and immortal.

1.52.s:
trayodaśasahasrāṇi varṣāṇāṃ te narottamāḥ
āyuḥpramāṇaṃ jīvanti varṣe divye tvilāvṛte //
1.52.d:
त्रयोदशसहस्राणि वर्षाणां ते नरोत्तमाः
आयुःप्रमाणं जीवन्ति वर्षे दिव्ये त्विलावृते ॥
1.52.m: For thirteen thousand years those best of men / live as the measure of their lifespan in the divine Ilāvṛta region.

1.52.s:
jaṃbūphalarasaṃ pītvā na jarā bādhate tvimān
na kṣudhā na klamaścāpi na jano mṛtyumāṃs tathā //
1.52.d:
जंबूफलरसं पीत्वा न जरा बाधते त्विमान्
न क्षुधा न क्लमश्चापि न जनो मृत्युमांस् तथा ॥
1.52.m: Having drunk the juice of the jambu fruit, old age does not afflict them, / nor hunger, nor fatigue, nor does that person suffer death.

1.52.s:
tatra jāmbūnadaṃ nāma kanakaṃ devabhūṣaṇam
indragopapratīkāśaṃ jāyate bhāsvaraṃ tu tat //
1.52.d:
तत्र जाम्बूनदं नाम कनकं देवभूषणम्
इन्द्रगोपप्रतीकाशं जायते भास्वरं तु तत् ॥
1.52.m: There is produced the gold called Jāmbūnada, an ornament for the gods, / resembling an indragopa insect, truly lustrous.

1.52.s:
evaṃ mayā samākhyātā navavarṣānuvartinaḥ
varṇāyurbhojanādyāni saṃkṣipya na tu vistarāt //
1.52.d:
एवं मया समाख्याता नववर्षानुवर्तिनः
वर्णायुर्भोजनाद्यानि संक्षिप्य न तु विस्तरात् ॥
1.52.m: Thus the inhabitants of the nine regions have been declared by me, / their castes, lifespans, foods, and the rest, briefly and not at length.

1.52.s:
hemakūṭe tu gandharvā vijñeyāścāpsarogaṇāḥ
sarve nāgāś ca niṣadhe śeṣavāsukitakṣakāḥ //
1.52.d:
हेमकूटे तु गन्धर्वा विज्ञेयाश्चाप्सरोगणाः
सर्वे नागाश् च निषधे शेषवासुकितक्षकाः ॥
1.52.m: On Hemakūṭa are to be known Gandharvas and hosts of Apsarases; / on Niṣadha are all the serpents—Śeṣa, Vāsuki, and Takṣaka.

1.52.s:
mahābalās trayastriṃśad ramante yājñikāḥ surāḥ
nīle tu vaiḍūryamaye siddhā brahmarṣayo 'malāḥ //
1.52.d:
महाबलास् त्रयस्त्रिंशद् रमन्ते याज्ञिकाः सुराः
नीले तु वैडूर्यमये सिद्धा ब्रह्मर्षयो ऽमलाः ॥
1.52.m: The thirty-three sacrificial gods of great might take their delight [there]; / while on Nīla, which is made of lapis lazuli, are the spotless Siddhas and brahmin seers.

1.52.s:
daityānāṃ dānavānāṃ ca śvetaḥ parvata ucyate
śṛṅgavān parvataścaiva pitṝṇāṃ nilayaḥ sadā //
1.52.d:
दैत्यानां दानवानां च श्वेतः पर्वत उच्यते
शृङ्गवान् पर्वतश्चैव पितॄणां निलयः सदा ॥
1.52.m: Mount Śveta is said to be the abode of Daityas and Dānavas; / and Mount Śṛṅgavān is the perpetual dwelling-place of the ancestors.

1.52.s:
himavān yakṣamukhyānāṃ bhūtānām īśvarasya ca
sarvādriṣu mahādevo hariṇā brahmaṇāṃbayā //
1.52.d:
हिमवान् यक्षमुख्यानां भूतानाम् ईश्वरस्य च
सर्वाद्रिषु महादेवो हरिणा ब्रह्मणांबया ॥
1.52.m: Himavān is the abode of chief Yakṣas, spirits, and the Lord. / On all mountains is Mahādeva, along with Hari, Brahmā, and the Mother,

1.52.s:
nandinā ca gaṇaiścaiva varṣeṣu ca vaneṣu ca
nīlaśvetatriśṛṅge ca bhagavānnīlalohitaḥ //
1.52.d:
नन्दिना च गणैश्चैव वर्षेषु च वनेषु च
नीलश्वेतत्रिशृङ्गे च भगवान्नीललोहितः ॥
1.52.m: along with Nandin and the gaṇas, in the regions and in the forests; / and on Nīla, Śveta, and Triśṛṅga, the lord Nīlalohita

1.52.s:
siddhairdevaiś ca pitṛbhir dṛṣṭo nityaṃ viśeṣataḥ
nīlaś ca vaiḍūryamayaḥ śvetaḥ śuklo hiraṇmayaḥ //
1.52.d:
सिद्धैर्देवैश् च पितृभिर् दृष्टो नित्यं विशेषतः
नीलश् च वैडूर्यमयः श्वेतः शुक्लो हिरण्मयः ॥
1.52.m: is seen constantly, especially by Siddhas, gods, and ancestors. / Nīla is made of lapis lazuli, Śveta is white and golden;

1.52.s:
mayūrabarhavarṇastu śātakuṃbhas triśṛṅgavān
ete parvatarājāno jaṃbūdvīpe vyavasthitāḥ //
1.52.d:
मयूरबर्हवर्णस्तु शातकुंभस् त्रिशृङ्गवान्
एते पर्वतराजानो जंबूद्वीपे व्यवस्थिताः ॥
1.52.m: Triśṛṅgavān is made of gold, with the color of a peacock's feather. / These kingly mountains are situated in Jambūdvīpa.

1.53.s:
sūta uvāca
plakṣadvīpādidvīpeṣu sapta saptasu parvatāḥ
ṛjvāyatāḥ pratidiśaṃ niviṣṭā varṣaparvatāḥ //
1.53.d:
सूत उवाच
प्लक्षद्वीपादिद्वीपेषु सप्त सप्तसु पर्वताः
ऋज्वायताः प्रतिदिशं निविष्टा वर्षपर्वताः ॥
1.53.m: Sūta said: / In the seven continents beginning with Plakṣadvīpa, there are seven mountains in each, / straight and extended, situated in each direction as boundary mountains.

1.53.s:
plakṣadvīpe tu vakṣyāmi sapta divyān mahācalān
gomedako 'tra prathamo dvitīyaścāndra ucyate //
1.53.d:
प्लक्षद्वीपे तु वक्ष्यामि सप्त दिव्यान् महाचलान्
गोमेदको ऽत्र प्रथमो द्वितीयश्चान्द्र उच्यते ॥
1.53.m:
Now I shall describe the seven divine great mountains on Plakṣadvīpa:
Gomedaka is the first here, and the second is called Cāndra;

1.53.s:
tṛtīyo nārado nāma caturtho dundubhiḥ smṛtaḥ
pañcamaḥ somako nāma sumanāḥ ṣaṣṭha ucyate //
1.53.d:
तृतीयो नारदो नाम चतुर्थो दुन्दुभिः स्मृतः
पञ्चमः सोमको नाम सुमनाः षष्ठ उच्यते ॥
1.53.m:
The third is named Nārada; the fourth is remembered as Dundubhi;
The fifth is named Somaka, and the sixth is called Sumanas;

1.53.s:
sa eva vaibhavaḥ prokto vaibhrājaḥ saptamaḥ smṛtaḥ
saptaite girayaḥ proktāḥ plakṣadvīpe viśeṣataḥ //
1.53.d:
स एव वैभवः प्रोक्तो वैभ्राजः सप्तमः स्मृतः
सप्तैते गिरयः प्रोक्ताः प्लक्षद्वीपे विशेषतः ॥
1.53.m:
It is also declared to be Vaibhava, and the seventh is remembered as Vaibhrāja.
These seven mountains are especially proclaimed on Plakṣadvīpa.

1.53.s:
sapta vai śālmalidvīpe tāṃstu vakṣyāmyanukramāt
kumudaścottamaścaiva parvataś ca balāhakaḥ //
1.53.d:
सप्त वै शाल्मलिद्वीपे तांस्तु वक्ष्याम्यनुक्रमात्
कुमुदश्चोत्तमश्चैव पर्वतश् च बलाहकः ॥
1.53.m:
There are indeed seven on Śālmalidvīpa, and I shall describe them in order:
Kumuda, Uttama, and the mountain Balāhaka,

1.53.s:
droṇaḥ kaṅkaś ca mahiṣaḥ kakudmān saptamaḥ smṛtaḥ
kuśadvīpe tu saptaiva dvīpāś ca kulaparvatāḥ //
1.53.d:
द्रोणः कङ्कश् च महिषः ककुद्मान् सप्तमः स्मृतः
कुशद्वीपे तु सप्तैव द्वीपाश् च कुलपर्वताः ॥
1.53.m:
Droṇa, Kaṅka, Mahiṣa, and Kakudmat is remembered as the seventh.
On Kuśadvīpa there are seven clan-mountains:

1.53.s:
tāṃstu saṃkṣepato vakṣye nāmamātreṇa vai kramāt
vidrumaḥ prathamaḥ prokto dvitīyo hemaparvataḥ //
1.53.d:
तांस्तु संक्षेपतो वक्ष्ये नाममात्रेण वै क्रमात्
विद्रुमः प्रथमः प्रोक्तो द्वितीयो हेमपर्वतः ॥
1.53.m:
I shall state them concisely, indeed, by name alone in order:
Vidruma is proclaimed the first, the second is the mountain Hema,

1.53.s:
tṛtīyo dyutimānnāma caturthaḥ puṣpitaḥ smṛtaḥ
kuśeśayaḥ pañcamastu ṣaṣṭho harigiriḥ smṛtaḥ //
1.53.d:
तृतीयो द्युतिमान्नाम चतुर्थः पुष्पितः स्मृतः
कुशेशयः पञ्चमस्तु षष्ठो हरिगिरिः स्मृतः ॥
1.53.m:
The third is named Dyutimat, the fourth is remembered as Puṣpita,
The fifth is Kuśeśaya, and the sixth is remembered as Harigiri;

1.53.s:
saptamo mandaraḥ śrīmān mahādevaniketanam
mandā iti hyapāṃ nāma mandaro dhāraṇād apām //
1.53.d:
सप्तमो मन्दरः श्रीमान् महादेवनिकेतनम्
मन्दा इति ह्यपां नाम मन्दरो धारणाद् अपाम् ॥
1.53.m:
The seventh is the glorious Mandara, the abode of Mahādeva.
For 'mandāḥ' is the name of the waters; it is called Mandara because it holds the waters.

1.53.s:
tatra sākṣādvṛṣāṅkastu viśveśo vimalaḥ śivaḥ
somaḥ sanandī bhagavān āste hemagṛhottame //
1.53.d:
तत्र साक्षाद्वृषाङ्कस्तु विश्वेशो विमलः शिवः
सोमः सनन्दी भगवान् आस्ते हेमगृहोत्तमे ॥
1.53.m:
There the bull-bannered Lord Śiva himself, spotless Lord of All,
Accompanied by Umā and Nandin, resides in an excellent golden palace.

1.53.s:
tapasā toṣitaḥ pūrvaṃ mandareṇa maheśvaraḥ
avimukte mahākṣetre lebhe sa paramaṃ varam //
1.53.d:
तपसा तोषितः पूर्वं मन्दरेण महेश्वरः
अविमुक्ते महाक्षेत्रे लेभे स परमं वरम् ॥
1.53.m:
Maheśvara, formerly pleased by the ascetic penance of Mandara
In the great sacred site of Avimukta, granted him a supreme boon.

1.53.s:
prārthitaś ca mahādevo nivāsārthaṃ sahāṃbayā
avimuktādupāgamya cakre vāsaṃ sa mandare //
1.53.d:
प्रार्थितश् च महादेवो निवासार्थं सहांबया
अविमुक्तादुपागम्य चक्रे वासं स मन्दरे ॥
1.53.m:
Mahādeva, being besought to dwell [there] together with the Mother,
Came from Avimukta and took up his residence on Mandara.

1.53.s:
sanandī sagaṇaḥ somas tenāsau tanna muñcati
krauñcadvīpe tu sapteha krauñcādyāḥ kulaparvatāḥ //
1.53.d:
सनन्दी सगणः सोमस् तेनासौ तन्न मुञ्चति
क्रौञ्चद्वीपे तु सप्तेह क्रौञ्चाद्याः कुलपर्वताः ॥
1.53.m:
Accompanied by Nandin, by his attendants, and by Umā, he therefore does not leave it.
On Krauñcadvīpa here, there are seven clan-mountains beginning with Krauñca:

1.53.s:
krauñco vāmanakaḥ paścāt tṛtīyaścāndhakārakaḥ
andhakārātparaścāpi divāvṛnnāma parvataḥ //
1.53.d:
क्रौञ्चो वामनकः पश्चात् तृतीयश्चान्धकारकः
अन्धकारात्परश्चापि दिवावृन्नाम पर्वतः ॥
1.53.m:
Krauñca, next Vāmanaka, and third Andhakāraka;
Beyond Andhakāra is also the mountain named Divāvṛt;

1.53.s:
divāvṛtaḥ paraścāpi vivindo girirucyate
vivindātparataścāpi puṇḍarīko mahāgiriḥ //
1.53.d:
दिवावृतः परश्चापि विविन्दो गिरिरुच्यते
विविन्दात्परतश्चापि पुण्डरीको महागिरिः ॥
1.53.m:
Beyond Divāvṛta the mountain is called Vivinda;
And beyond Vivinda is the great mountain Puṇḍarīka;

1.53.s:
puṇḍarīkātparaścāpi procyate dundubhisvanaḥ
ete ratnamayāḥ sapta krauñcadvīpasya parvatāḥ //
1.53.d:
पुण्डरीकात्परश्चापि प्रोच्यते दुन्दुभिस्वनः
एते रत्नमयाः सप्त क्रौञ्चद्वीपस्य पर्वताः ॥
1.53.m:
Beyond Puṇḍarīka is declared Dundubhisvana.
These are the seven jewel-formed mountains of Krauñcadvīpa.

1.53.s:
śākadvīpe ca girayaḥ sapta tāṃstu nibodhata
udayo raivataścāpi śyāmako munisattamāḥ //
1.53.d:
शाकद्वीपे च गिरयः सप्त तांस्तु निबोधत
उदयो रैवतश्चापि श्यामको मुनिसत्तमाः ॥
1.53.m:
Learn of the seven mountains on Śākadvīpa, O best of sages:
Udaya, Raivata, and Śyāmaka, O best of sages,

1.53.s:
rājataśca giriḥ śrīmān āṃbikeyaḥ suśobhanaḥ
āṃbikeyātparo ramyaḥ sarvauṣadhisamanvitaḥ //
1.53.d:
राजतश्च गिरिः श्रीमान् आंबिकेयः सुशोभनः
आंबिकेयात्परो रम्यः सर्वौषधिसमन्वितः ॥
1.53.m:
The glorious mountain Rājata, the very beautiful Āmbikeya,
Beyond Āmbikeya the delightful [mountain] endowed with all medicinal herbs,

1.53.s:
tathaiva kesarītyukto yato vāyuḥ prajāyate
puṣkare parvataḥ śrīmān eka eva mahāśilaḥ //
1.53.d:
तथैव केसरीत्युक्तो यतो वायुः प्रजायते
पुष्करे पर्वतः श्रीमान् एक एव महाशिलः ॥
1.53.m:
And likewise the one called Kesarī, from which the wind arises.
On Puṣkara there is only one glorious mountain, a single great rock,

1.53.s:
citrairmaṇimayaiḥ kūṭaiḥ śilājālaiḥ samucchritaiḥ
dvīpasya tasya pūrvārdhe citrasānusthito mahān //
1.53.d:
चित्रैर्मणिमयैः कूटैः शिलाजालैः समुच्छ्रितैः
द्वीपस्य तस्य पूर्वार्धे चित्रसानुस्थितो महान् ॥
1.53.m:
With variegated jewelled peaks and lofty masses of rock.
On the eastern half of that continent stands the great [mountain] with variegated ridges,

1.53.s:
yojanānāṃ sahasrāṇi ūrdhvaṃ pañcāśaducchritaḥ
adhaścaiva catustriṃśat sahasrāṇi mahācalaḥ //
1.53.d:
योजनानां सहस्राणि ऊर्ध्वं पञ्चाशदुच्छ्रितः
अधश्चैव चतुस्त्रिंशत् सहस्राणि महाचलः ॥
1.53.m:
Rising upwards fifty thousand yojanas,
And thirty-four thousand [yojanas] below, a great mountain.

1.53.s:
dvīpasyārdhe parikṣiptaḥ parvato mānasottaraḥ
sthito velāsamīpe tu navacandra ivoditaḥ //
1.53.d:
द्वीपस्यार्धे परिक्षिप्तः पर्वतो मानसोत्तरः
स्थितो वेलासमीपे तु नवचन्द्र इवोदितः ॥
1.53.m:
Surrounding half of the continent stands the mountain Mānasottara,
Situated near the shore like the newly risen moon.

1.53.s:
yojanānāṃ sahasrāṇi ūrdhvaṃ pañcāśaducchritaḥ
tāvadeva tu vistīrṇaḥ pārśvataḥ parimaṇḍalaḥ //
1.53.d:
योजनानां सहस्राणि ऊर्ध्वं पञ्चाशदुच्छ्रितः
तावदेव तु विस्तीर्णः पार्श्वतः परिमण्डलः ॥
1.53.m:
It rises upwards fifty thousand yojanas,
And is just as broad sideways, forming a circle.

1.53.s:
sa eva dvīpapaścārdhe mānasaḥ pṛthivīdharaḥ
eka eva mahāsānuḥ saṃniveśāddvidhā kṛtaḥ //
1.53.d:
स एव द्वीपपश्चार्धे मानसः पृथिवीधरः
एक एव महासानुः संनिवेशाद्द्विधा कृतः ॥
1.53.m:
It is the very same mountain Mānasa on the western half of the continent;
It is a single great-ridged mountain, divided into two by its disposition.

1.53.s:
tasmindvīpe smṛtau dvau tu puṇyau janapadau śubhau
rājatau mānasasyātha parvatasyānumaṇḍalau //
1.53.d:
तस्मिन्द्वीपे स्मृतौ द्वौ तु पुण्यौ जनपदौ शुभौ
राजतौ मानसस्याथ पर्वतस्यानुमण्डलौ ॥
1.53.m:
In that continent are remembered two auspicious, meritorious realms,
Resplendent, following the circular form of Mount Mānasa:

1.53.s:
mahāvītaṃ tu yadvarṣaṃ bāhyato mānasasya tu
tasyaivābhyantaro yastu dhātakīkhaṇḍa ucyate //
1.53.d:
महावीतं तु यद्वर्षं बाह्यतो मानसस्य तु
तस्यैवाभ्यन्तरो यस्तु धातकीखण्ड उच्यते ॥
1.53.m:
The realm outside Mānasa is Mahāvīta,
While the one inside it is called Dhātakīkhaṇḍa.

1.53.s:
svādūdakenodadhinā puṣkaraḥ parivāritaḥ
puṣkaradvīpavistāravistīrṇo 'sau samantataḥ //
1.53.d:
स्वादूदकेनोदधिना पुष्करः परिवारितः
पुष्करद्वीपविस्तारविस्तीर्णो ऽसौ समन्ततः ॥
1.53.m:
Puṣkara is surrounded by the ocean of sweet water,
Which extends all around equal to the width of Puṣkaradvīpa.

1.53.s:
vistārānmaṇḍalāccaiva puṣkarasya samena tu
evaṃ dvīpāḥ samudraistu saptasaptabhir āvṛtāḥ //
1.53.d:
विस्तारान्मण्डलाच्चैव पुष्करस्य समेन तु
एवं द्वीपाः समुद्रैस्तु सप्तसप्तभिर् आवृताः ॥
1.53.m:
In its width and circumference it is equal to Puṣkara;
In this manner the continents are surrounded by the seven oceans, each by each.

1.53.s:
dvīpasyānantaro yastu samudraḥ saptamastu vai
evaṃ dvīpasamudrāṇāṃ vṛddhirjñeyā parasparam //
1.53.d:
द्वीपस्यानन्तरो यस्तु समुद्रः सप्तमस्तु वै
एवं द्वीपसमुद्राणां वृद्धिर्ज्ञेया परस्परम् ॥
1.53.m:
The ocean contiguous to the continent is the seventh;
Thus an equal increase between the continents and oceans should be known.

1.53.s:
pareṇa puṣkarasyātha anuvṛtya sthito mahān
svādūdakasamudrastu samantātpariveṣṭya ca //
1.53.d:
परेण पुष्करस्याथ अनुवृत्य स्थितो महान्
स्वादूदकसमुद्रस्तु समन्तात्परिवेष्ट्य च ॥
1.53.m:
Beyond Puṣkara, the great ocean of sweet water
Stands following it, encircling it on all sides.

1.53.s:
pareṇa tasya mahatī dṛśyate lokasaṃsthitiḥ
kāñcanī dviguṇā bhūmiḥ sarvā caikaśilopamā //
1.53.d:
परेण तस्य महती दृश्यते लोकसंस्थितिः
काञ्चनी द्विगुणा भूमिः सर्वा चैकशिलोपमा ॥
1.53.m:
Beyond that, the great extent of the universe is seen:
A golden land of twice the size, all resembling a single stone.

1.53.s:
tasyāḥ pareṇa śailastu maryādāpāramaṇḍalaḥ
prakāśaścāprakāśaś ca lokālokaḥ sa ucyate //
1.53.d:
तस्याः परेण शैलस्तु मर्यादापारमण्डलः
प्रकाशश्चाप्रकाशश् च लोकालोकः स उच्यते ॥
1.53.m:
Beyond that is the mountain that forms the limiting boundary-ring;
It is light and darkness, and is called Lokāloka.

1.53.s:
dṛśyādṛśyagirir yāvat tāvadeṣā dharā dvijāḥ
yojanānāṃ sahasrāṇi daśa tasyocchrayaḥ smṛtaḥ //
1.53.d:
दृश्यादृश्यगिरिर् यावत् तावदेषा धरा द्विजाः
योजनानां सहस्राणि दश तस्योच्छ्रयः स्मृतः ॥
1.53.m:
As far as the mountain of the visible and invisible extends, so far is this earth, O twice-born.
Its height is remembered to be ten thousand yojanas,

1.53.s:
tāvāṃś ca vistarastasya lokālokamahāgireḥ
arvācīne tu tasyārdhe caranti raviraśmayaḥ //
1.53.d:
तावांश् च विस्तरस्तस्य लोकालोकमहागिरेः
अर्वाचीने तु तस्यार्धे चरन्ति रविरश्मयः ॥
1.53.m:
And such is the breadth of that great mountain Lokāloka.
The rays of the sun travel over its inner half,

1.53.s:
parārdhe tu tamo nityaṃ lokālokastataḥ smṛtaḥ
evaṃ saṃkṣepataḥ prokto bhūrlokasya ca vistaraḥ //
1.53.d:
परार्धे तु तमो नित्यं लोकालोकस्ततः स्मृतः
एवं संक्षेपतः प्रोक्तो भूर्लोकस्य च विस्तरः ॥
1.53.m:
While darkness is eternal on its outer half; therefore it is remembered as Lokāloka.
Thus the extent of Bhūrloka has been stated in brief.

1.53.s:
ā bhānorvai bhuvaḥ svastu ā dhruvānmunisattamāḥ
āvahādyā niviṣṭāstu vāyorvai sapta nemayaḥ //
1.53.d:
आ भानोर्वै भुवः स्वस्तु आ ध्रुवान्मुनिसत्तमाः
आवहाद्या निविष्टास्तु वायोर्वै सप्त नेमयः ॥
1.53.m:
Bhuvarloka extends up to the sun, and Svarloka up to Dhruva, O best of sages.
The seven rims of wind, beginning with Āvaha, are situated [there]:

1.53.s:
āvahaḥ pravahaścaiva tataścānuvahas tathā
saṃvaho vivahaścātha tataścordhvaṃ parāvahaḥ //
1.53.d:
आवहः प्रवहश्चैव ततश्चानुवहस् तथा
संवहो विवहश्चाथ ततश्चोर्ध्वं परावहः ॥
1.53.m:
Āvaha, Pravaha, and next Anuvaha,
Saṃvaha, Vivaha, and above that Parāvaha,

1.53.s:
dvijāḥ parivahaśceti vāyorvai sapta nemayaḥ
balāhakās tathā bhānuś candro nakṣatrarāśayaḥ //
1.53.d:
द्विजाः परिवहश्चेति वायोर्वै सप्त नेमयः
बलाहकास् तथा भानुश् चन्द्रो नक्षत्रराशयः ॥
1.53.m:
And, O twice-born, Parivaha; these are indeed the seven rims of wind.
The rain-clouds, the sun, the moon, the constellations,

1.53.s:
grahāṇi ṛṣayaḥ sapta dhruvo viprāḥ kramādiha
yojanānāṃ mahīpṛṣṭhād ūrdhvaṃ pañcadaśa ā dhruvāt //
1.53.d:
ग्रहाणि ऋषयः सप्त ध्रुवो विप्राः क्रमादिह
योजनानां महीपृष्ठाद् ऊर्ध्वं पञ्चदश आ ध्रुवात् ॥
1.53.m:
The planets, the seven sages, and Dhruva, O brahmins, are here in succession.
Upwards from the surface of the earth to Dhruva is fifteen

1.53.s:
niyutānyekaniyutaṃ bhūpṛṣṭhādbhānumaṇḍalam
rathaḥ ṣoḍaśasāhasro bhāskarasya tathopari //
1.53.d:
नियुतान्येकनियुतं भूपृष्ठाद्भानुमण्डलम्
रथः षोडशसाहस्रो भास्करस्य तथोपरि ॥
1.53.m:
Hundred-thousands of yojanas; from the surface of the earth the solar disc is one hundred thousand.
The chariot of the sun above is sixteen thousand [yojanas],

1.53.s:
caturaśītisāhasro meruścopari bhūtalāt
koṭiyojanamākramya maharloko dhruvāddhruvaḥ //
1.53.d:
चतुरशीतिसाहस्रो मेरुश्चोपरि भूतलात्
कोटियोजनमाक्रम्य महर्लोको ध्रुवाद्ध्रुवः ॥
1.53.m:
And Meru above the surface of the earth is eighty-four thousand.
Covering one crore of yojanas from Dhruva is the fixed Maharloka;

1.53.s:
janaloko maharlokāt tathā koṭidvayaṃ dvijāḥ
janalokāttapolokaś catasraḥ koṭayo mataḥ //
1.53.d:
जनलोको महर्लोकात् तथा कोटिद्वयं द्विजाः
जनलोकात्तपोलोकश् चतस्रः कोटयो मतः ॥
1.53.m:
Janaloka is two crores [of yojanas] from Maharloka, O twice-born;
Tapoloka is considered to be four crores from Janaloka;

1.53.s:
prājāpatyādbrahmalokaḥ koṭiṣaṭkaṃ visṛjya tu
puṇyalokāstu saptaite hy aṇḍe 'sminkathitā dvijāḥ //
1.53.d:
प्राजापत्याद्ब्रह्मलोकः कोटिषट्कं विसृज्य तु
पुण्यलोकास्तु सप्तैते ह्य् अण्डे ऽस्मिन्कथिता द्विजाः ॥
1.53.m:
Leaving six crores beyond Prājāpatya is Brahmaloka.
These seven meritorious worlds within this cosmic egg have thus been told, O twice-born.

1.53.s:
adhaḥ saptatalānāṃ tu narakāṇāṃ hi koṭayaḥ
māyāntāścaiva ghorādyā aṣṭāviṃśatireva tu //
1.53.d:
अधः सप्ततलानां तु नरकाणां हि कोटयः
मायान्ताश्चैव घोराद्या अष्टाविंशतिरेव तु ॥
1.53.m:
Below the seven underworlds are crores of hells,
Beginning with Ghora and ending with Māyā, twenty-eight in number.

1.53.s:
pāpinasteṣu pacyante svasvakarmānurūpataḥ
avīcyantāni sarvāṇi rauravādyāni teṣu ca //
1.53.d:
पापिनस्तेषु पच्यन्ते स्वस्वकर्मानुरूपतः
अवीच्यन्तानि सर्वाणि रौरवाद्यानि तेषु च ॥
1.53.m:
In them sinners are roasted according to their respective actions;
Among them, all [hells] beginning with Raurava and ending with Avīci

1.53.s:
pratyekaṃ pañcakānyāhur narakāṇi viśeṣataḥ
aṇḍamādau mayā proktam aṇḍasyāvaraṇāni ca //
1.53.d:
प्रत्येकं पञ्चकान्याहुर् नरकाणि विशेषतः
अण्डमादौ मया प्रोक्तम् अण्डस्यावरणानि च ॥
1.53.m:
Are each said specifically to be groups of five hells.
At first the cosmic egg was declared by me, as well as the coverings of the cosmic egg,

1.53.s:
hiraṇyagarbhasargaś ca prasaṃgādbahuvistarāt
aṇḍānāmīdṛśānāṃ tu koṭyo jñeyāḥ sahasraśaḥ //
1.53.d:
हिरण्यगर्भसर्गश् च प्रसंगाद्बहुविस्तरात्
अण्डानामीदृशानां तु कोट्यो ज्ञेयाः सहस्रशः ॥
1.53.m:
And the creation of Hiraṇyagarbha, extensively in that connection.
Crores and thousands of such cosmic eggs are to be known,

1.53.s:
sarvagatvāt pradhānasya tiryag ūrdhvam adhas tathā
aṇḍeṣveteṣu sarveṣu bhuvanāni caturdaśa //
1.53.d:
सर्वगत्वात् प्रधानस्य तिर्यग् ऊर्ध्वम् अधस् तथा
अण्डेष्वेतेषु सर्वेषु भुवनानि चतुर्दश ॥
1.53.m:
Because Pradhāna is all-pervading horizontally, upwards, and downwards.
In all these cosmic eggs there are fourteen worlds

1.53.s:
pratyaṇḍaṃ dvijaśārdūlās teṣāṃ heturmaheśvaraḥ
aṇḍeṣu cāṇḍabāhyeṣu tathāṇḍāvaraṇeṣu ca //
1.53.d:
प्रत्यण्डं द्विजशार्दूलास् तेषां हेतुर्महेश्वरः
अण्डेषु चाण्डबाह्येषु तथाण्डावरणेषु च ॥
1.53.m:
In each cosmic egg, O tigers among the twice-born, and Maheśvara is their cause.
Within the cosmic eggs, outside the cosmic eggs, and in the coverings of the cosmic eggs,

1.53.s:
tamo 'nte ca tamaḥpāre cāṣṭamūrtirvyavasthitaḥ
asyātmano maheśasya mahādevasya dhīmataḥ //
1.53.d:
तमो ऽन्ते च तमःपारे चाष्टमूर्तिर्व्यवस्थितः
अस्यात्मनो महेशस्य महादेवस्य धीमतः ॥
1.53.m:
At the end of darkness and beyond darkness, he who has eight forms is situated.
Of this Self, of the wise Maheśa, of Mahādeva—

1.53.s:
adehinas tvaho deham akhilaṃ paramātmanaḥ
asyāṣṭamūrteḥ śarvasya śivasya gṛhamedhinaḥ //
1.53.d:
अदेहिनस् त्वहो देहम् अखिलं परमात्मनः
अस्याष्टमूर्तेः शर्वस्य शिवस्य गृहमेधिनः ॥
1.53.m: Though he is bodiless, behold, this entire [universe] is the body of the Supreme Self, / of this eight-formed Śarva, of Śiva the householder.

1.53.s:
gṛhiṇī prakṛtirdivyā prajāś ca mahadādayaḥ
paśavaḥ kiṅkarāstasya sarve dehābhimāninaḥ //
1.53.d:
गृहिणी प्रकृतिर्दिव्या प्रजाश् च महदादयः
पशवः किङ्करास्तस्य सर्वे देहाभिमानिनः ॥
1.53.m: His divine wife is Prakṛti, and his offspring are Mahat and the rest. / All embodied beings with ego are his beasts and servants.

1.53.s:
ādyantahīno bhagavān anantaḥ pumānpradhānapramukhāś ca sapta
pradhānamūrtistvatha ṣoḍaśāṅgo maheśvaraścāṣṭatanuḥ sa eva //
1.53.d:
आद्यन्तहीनो भगवान् अनन्तः पुमान्प्रधानप्रमुखाश् च सप्त
प्रधानमूर्तिस्त्वथ षोडशाङ्गो महेश्वरश्चाष्टतनुः स एव ॥
1.53.m: The Lord is without beginning or end, infinite, the Puruṣa; the seven principles beginning with Pradhāna [are his bodies]; / his form is Pradhāna, he has sixteen limbs, and he alone is Maheśvara of eight forms.

1.53.s:
ājñābalāttasya dharā sthiteha dharādharā vāridharāḥ samudrāḥ
jyotirgaṇaḥ śakramukhāḥ surāś ca vaimānikāḥ sthāvarajaṅgamāś ca //
1.53.d:
आज्ञाबलात्तस्य धरा स्थितेह धराधरा वारिधराः समुद्राः
ज्योतिर्गणः शक्रमुखाः सुराश् च वैमानिकाः स्थावरजङ्गमाश् च ॥
1.53.m: By the power of his command the earth stands here, as do the mountains, clouds, and oceans, / the host of luminaries, the gods headed by Indra, those who travel in aerial chariots, and all things moving and unmoving.

1.53.s:
dṛṣṭvā yakṣaṃ lakṣaṇairhīnamīśaṃ dṛṣṭvā sendrāste kimetattviheti
yakṣaṃ gatvā niścayātpāvakādyāḥ śaktikṣīṇāścābhavan yattato 'pi //
1.53.d:
दृष्ट्वा यक्षं लक्षणैर्हीनमीशं दृष्ट्वा सेन्द्रास्ते किमेतत्त्विहेति
यक्षं गत्वा निश्चयात्पावकाद्याः शक्तिक्षीणाश्चाभवन् यत्ततो ऽपि ॥
1.53.m: Having seen a yakṣa, the Lord devoid of [manifest] marks, Indra and the gods wondered, 'What is this here?' / Approaching the yakṣa to determine [its nature], Fire and the other gods became devoid of their powers, and even from that [moment]—

1.53.s:
dagdhuṃ tṛṇaṃ vāpi samakṣamasya yakṣasya vahnirna śaśāka viprāḥ
vāyustṛṇaṃ cālayituṃ tathānye svānsvānprabhāvān sakalāmarendrāḥ //
1.53.d:
दग्धुं तृणं वापि समक्षमस्य यक्षस्य वह्निर्न शशाक विप्राः
वायुस्तृणं चालयितुं तथान्ये स्वान्स्वान्प्रभावान् सकलामरेन्द्राः ॥
1.53.m: O brahmins, Fire was unable even to burn a blade of grass before this yakṣa, / Wind [was unable] to move a blade of grass, and so too all the other lords of the immortals [lost] their respective powers.

1.53.s:
tadā svayaṃ vṛtraripuḥ surendraiḥ sureśvaraḥ sarvasamṛddhihetuḥ
sureśvaraṃ yakṣamuvāca ko vā bhavānitītthaṃ sa kutūhalātmā //
1.53.d:
तदा स्वयं वृत्ररिपुः सुरेन्द्रैः सुरेश्वरः सर्वसमृद्धिहेतुः
सुरेश्वरं यक्षमुवाच को वा भवानितीत्थं स कुतूहलात्मा ॥
1.53.m: Then the enemy of Vṛtra himself, the lord of the gods, the cause of all prosperity, / filled with curiosity, said to that lord of the gods, the yakṣa: 'Who are you?'

1.53.s:
tadā hyadṛśyaṃ gata eva yakṣas tadāṃbikā haimavatī śubhāsyā
umā śubhairābharaṇairanekaiḥ suśobhamānā tvanu cāvirāsīt //
1.53.d:
तदा ह्यदृश्यं गत एव यक्षस् तदांबिका हैमवती शुभास्या
उमा शुभैराभरणैरनेकैः सुशोभमाना त्वनु चाविरासीत् ॥
1.53.m: Then indeed the yakṣa vanished; and thereupon Ambikā, the daughter of Himavat, of auspicious countenance, / Umā, shining splendidly with many auspicious ornaments, appeared in his wake.

1.53.s: kimetadīśe bahuśobhamāne vāṃbike yakṣavapuścakāsti //
1.53.d: किमेतदीशे बहुशोभमाने वांबिके यक्षवपुश्चकास्ति ॥
1.53.m: [Indra said:] 'What was this, O magnificent ruler, O Ambikā, that shone with the form of a yakṣa?'

1.53.s: praṇemurenāṃ mṛgarājagāminīmumāmajāṃ lohitaśuklakṛṣṇām //
1.53.d: प्रणेमुरेनां मृगराजगामिनीमुमामजां लोहितशुक्लकृष्णाम् ॥
1.53.m: They bowed to her, to Umā, who walks like the king of beasts, the unborn one who is red, white, and black.

1.53.s:
saṃbhāvitā sā sakalāmarendraiḥ sarvapravṛttistu surāsurāṇām
ahaṃ purāsaṃ prakṛtiś ca puṃso yakṣasya cājñāvaśagetyathāha //
1.53.d:
संभाविता सा सकलामरेन्द्रैः सर्वप्रवृत्तिस्तु सुरासुराणाम्
अहं पुरासं प्रकृतिश् च पुंसो यक्षस्य चाज्ञावशगेत्यथाह ॥
1.53.m: Honoured by all the lords of the immortals, she who is the source of all activity of gods and asuras / then said: 'In the beginning I was Prakṛti, subject to the command of the Puruṣa, the yakṣa.'

1.53.s:
tasmāddvijāḥ sarvamajasya tasya niyogataścāṇḍamabhūdajādvai
ajaś ca aṇḍādakhilaṃ ca tasmāj jyotirgaṇairlokamajātmakaṃ tat //
1.53.d:
तस्माद्द्विजाः सर्वमजस्य तस्य नियोगतश्चाण्डमभूदजाद्वै
अजश् च अण्डादखिलं च तस्माज् ज्योतिर्गणैर्लोकमजात्मकं तत् ॥
1.53.m: Therefore, O brahmins, everything came from that unborn one; by his command the cosmic egg arose from the unborn, / and from the egg arose the unborn [Brahmā], and from him this whole world consisting of luminaries, having the nature of the unborn.

1.54.s:
sūta uvāca
jyotirgaṇapracāraṃ vai saṃkṣipyāṇḍe bravīmyaham
devakṣetrāṇi cālokya grahacāraprasiddhaye //
1.54.d:
सूत उवाच
ज्योतिर्गणप्रचारं वै संक्षिप्याण्डे ब्रवीम्यहम्
देवक्षेत्राणि चालोक्य ग्रहचारप्रसिद्धये ॥
1.54.m: Sūta said: / I shall describe in brief the motion of the host of luminaries within the cosmic egg, / and observing the realms of the gods for the purpose of demonstrating the movements of the planets.

1.54.s:
mānasopari māhendrī prācyāṃ meroḥ purī sthitā
dakṣiṇe bhānuputrasya varuṇasya ca vāruṇī //
1.54.d:
मानसोपरि माहेन्द्री प्राच्यां मेरोः पुरी स्थिता
दक्षिणे भानुपुत्रस्य वरुणस्य च वारुणी ॥
1.54.m: Above the Mānasa mountain, on the east of Meru, lies the city of Indra; / in the south is that of the son of the Sun (Yama), and in the west that of Varuṇa.

1.54.s:
saumye somasya vipulā tāsu digdevatāḥ sthitāḥ
amarāvatī saṃyamanī sukhā caiva vibhā kramāt //
1.54.d:
सौम्ये सोमस्य विपुला तासु दिग्देवताः स्थिताः
अमरावती संयमनी सुखा चैव विभा क्रमात् ॥
1.54.m: In the north is the vast [city] of Soma; in these abide the guardians of the directions: / Amarāvatī, Saṃyamanī, Sukhā, and Vibhā, respectively.

1.54.s:
lokapālopariṣṭāt tu sarvato dakṣiṇāyane
kāṣṭhāṃ gatasya sūryasya gatir yā tāṃ nibodhata //
1.54.d:
लोकपालोपरिष्टात् तु सर्वतो दक्षिणायने
काष्ठां गतस्य सूर्यस्य गतिर् या तां निबोधत ॥
1.54.m: Above the world-protectors, everywhere during the southern course, / understand that motion of the sun when it has reached its limit:

1.54.s:
dakṣiṇaprakrame bhānuḥ kṣipteṣuriva dhāvati
jyotiṣāṃ cakramādāya satataṃ parigacchati //
1.54.d:
दक्षिणप्रक्रमे भानुः क्षिप्तेषुरिव धावति
ज्योतिषां चक्रमादाय सततं परिगच्छति ॥
1.54.m: In its southern course, the sun runs like an arrow discharged; / carrying the circle of luminaries, it continually moves around.

1.54.s:
purāntago yadā bhānuḥ śakrasya bhavati prabhuḥ
sarvaiḥ sāyamanaiḥ sauro hy udayo dṛśyate dvijāḥ //
1.54.d:
पुरान्तगो यदा भानुः शक्रस्य भवति प्रभुः
सर्वैः सायमनैः सौरो ह्य् उदयो दृश्यते द्विजाः ॥
1.54.m: When the sun, the lord, reaches the edge of the city of Indra, / the solar dawn is seen, O brahmins, by all the inhabitants of Saṃyamanī.

1.54.s:
sa eva sukhavatyāṃ tu niśāntasthaḥ pradṛśyate
astameti punaḥ sūryo vibhāyāṃ viśvadṛg vibhuḥ //
1.54.d:
स एव सुखवत्यां तु निशान्तस्थः प्रदृश्यते
अस्तमेति पुनः सूर्यो विभायां विश्वदृग् विभुः ॥
1.54.m: He himself is seen standing at the end of night in Sukhavatī; / and again the sun, the all-seeing lord, sets in Vibhā.

1.54.s:
mayā prokto 'marāvatyāṃ yathāsau vāritaskaraḥ
tathā saṃyamanīṃ prāpya sukhāṃ caiva vibhāṃ khagaḥ //
1.54.d:
मया प्रोक्तो ऽमरावत्यां यथासौ वारितस्करः
तथा संयमनीं प्राप्य सुखां चैव विभां खगः ॥
1.54.m: As this stealer of waters was described by me in Amarāvatī, / so the bird [of heaven] moves upon reaching Saṃyamanī, Sukhā, and Vibhā.

1.54.s:
yadāparāhṇastvāgneyyāṃ pūrvāhṇo nairṛte dvijāḥ
tadā tvapararātraś ca vāyubhāge sudāruṇaḥ //
1.54.d:
यदापराह्णस्त्वाग्नेय्यां पूर्वाह्णो नैरृते द्विजाः
तदा त्वपररात्रश् च वायुभागे सुदारुणः ॥
1.54.m: When it is afternoon in the south-east, it is forenoon in the south-west, O brahmins; / then it is the dread late night in the region of Vāyu (north-west).

1.54.s:
īśānyāṃ pūrvarātrastu gatireṣā ca sarvataḥ
evaṃ puṣkaramadhye tu yadā sarpati vāripaḥ //
1.54.d:
ईशान्यां पूर्वरात्रस्तु गतिरेषा च सर्वतः
एवं पुष्करमध्ये तु यदा सर्पति वारिपः ॥
1.54.m: In the north-east it is the early night, and this is the motion everywhere. / Thus when the drinker of water glides through the middle of Puṣkara,

1.54.s:
triṃśāṃśakaṃ tu medinyāṃ muhūrtenaiva gacchati
yojanānāṃ muhūrtasya imāṃ saṃkhyāṃ nibodhata //
1.54.d:
त्रिंशांशकं तु मेदिन्यां मुहूर्तेनैव गच्छति
योजनानां मुहूर्तस्य इमां संख्यां निबोधत ॥
1.54.m: he traverses a thirtieth part of the earth in a single muhūrta. / Understand this number of yojanas traversed in a muhūrta:

1.54.s:
pūrṇā śatasahasrāṇām ekatriṃśattu sā smṛtā
pañcāśacca tathānyāni sahasrāṇyadhikāni tu //
1.54.d:
पूर्णा शतसहस्राणाम् एकत्रिंशत्तु सा स्मृता
पञ्चाशच्च तथान्यानि सहस्राण्यधिकानि तु ॥
1.54.m: It is traditionally remembered as a full thirty-one hundred thousand (3,100,000), / and fifty thousand more besides (50,000).

1.54.s:
mauhūrtikī gatirhyeṣā bhāskarasya mahātmanaḥ
etena gatiyogena yadā kāṣṭhāṃ tu dakṣiṇām //
1.54.d:
मौहूर्तिकी गतिर्ह्येषा भास्करस्य महात्मनः
एतेन गतियोगेन यदा काष्ठां तु दक्षिणाम् ॥
1.54.m: Indeed, such is the hourly motion of the great-souled sun. / When, by this conjunction of motion, towards the southern limit

1.54.s:
paryapṛcchet pataṅgo 'pi saumyāśāṃ cottare 'hani
madhye tu puṣkarasyātha bhramate dakṣiṇāyane //
1.54.d:
पर्यपृच्छेत् पतङ्गो ऽपि सौम्याशां चोत्तरे ऽहनि
मध्ये तु पुष्करस्याथ भ्रमते दक्षिणायने ॥
1.54.m: the sun moves, and towards the northern quarter in the northern half of the year, / he roams in the middle of Puṣkara during the southern course.

1.54.s:
mānasottaraśaile tu mahātejā vibhāvasuḥ
maṇḍalānāṃ śataṃ pūrṇaṃ tadaśītyadhikaṃ vibhuḥ //
1.54.d:
मानसोत्तरशैले तु महातेजा विभावसुः
मण्डलानां शतं पूर्णं तदशीत्यधिकं विभुः ॥
1.54.m: Upon the Mānasottara mountain, the all-pervading sun of great splendour / [traverses] a full one hundred and eighty circuits.

1.54.s:
bāhyaṃ cābhyantaraṃ proktam uttarāyaṇadakṣiṇe
pratyahaṃ carate tāni sūryo vai maṇḍalāni tu //
1.54.d:
बाह्यं चाभ्यन्तरं प्रोक्तम् उत्तरायणदक्षिणे
प्रत्यहं चरते तानि सूर्यो वै मण्डलानि तु ॥
1.54.m: They are declared as outer and inner in the northern and southern courses; / each day the sun traverses those circuits.

1.54.s:
kulālacakraparyanto yathā śīghraṃ pravartate
dakṣiṇaprakrame devas tathā śīghraṃ pravartate //
1.54.d:
कुलालचक्रपर्यन्तो यथा शीघ्रं प्रवर्तते
दक्षिणप्रक्रमे देवस् तथा शीघ्रं प्रवर्तते ॥
1.54.m: Just as the outer rim of a potter's wheel revolves swiftly, / so the radiant deity moves swiftly in his southern course.

1.54.s:
tasmātprakṛṣṭāṃ bhūmiṃ tu kālenālpena gacchati
sūryo dvādaśabhiḥ śīghraṃ muhūrtairdakṣiṇāyane //
1.54.d:
तस्मात्प्रकृष्टां भूमिं तु कालेनाल्पेन गच्छति
सूर्यो द्वादशभिः शीघ्रं मुहूर्तैर्दक्षिणायने ॥
1.54.m: Therefore, in a short time he traverses a vast extent of the earth; / in his southern course the sun moves swiftly through twelve muhūrtas.

1.54.s:
trayodaśārdhamṛkṣāṇām ahnā tu carate raviḥ
muhūrtaistāvadṛkṣāṇi naktamaṣṭādaśaiścaran //
1.54.d:
त्रयोदशार्धमृक्षाणाम् अह्ना तु चरते रविः
मुहूर्तैस्तावदृक्षाणि नक्तमष्टादशैश्चरन् ॥
1.54.m: During the day the sun traverses thirteen and a half asterisms; / traversing as many asterisms during the night in eighteen muhūrtas.

1.54.s:
kulālacakramadhyaṃ tu yathā mandaṃ prasarpati
tathodagayane sūryaḥ sarpate mandavikramaḥ //
1.54.d:
कुलालचक्रमध्यं तु यथा मन्दं प्रसर्पति
तथोदगयने सूर्यः सर्पते मन्दविक्रमः ॥
1.54.m: Just as the centre of a potter's wheel revolves slowly, / so the sun glides in his northern course with slow progress.

1.54.s:
tasmāddīrgheṇa kālena bhūmimalpāṃ tu gacchati
sa ratho dhiṣṭhito bhānor ādityairmunibhis tathā //
1.54.d:
तस्माद्दीर्घेण कालेन भूमिमल्पां तु गच्छति
स रथो धिष्ठितो भानोर् आदित्यैर्मुनिभिस् तथा ॥
1.54.m: Therefore, in a long time he traverses a small extent of the earth. / That chariot of the sun is occupied by the Ādityas, by sages,

1.54.s:
gandharvairapsarobhiś ca grāmaṇīsarparākṣasaiḥ
pradīpayan sahasrāṃśur agrataḥ pṛṣṭhato 'pyadhaḥ //
1.54.d:
गन्धर्वैरप्सरोभिश् च ग्रामणीसर्पराक्षसैः
प्रदीपयन् सहस्रांशुर् अग्रतः पृष्ठतो ऽप्यधः ॥
1.54.m: by gandharvas, apsarases, village-leaders, serpents, and rākṣasas; / illuminating in front, behind, below, the thousand-rayed [sun],

1.54.s:
ūrdhvataś ca karaṃ tyaktvā sabhāṃ brāhmīmanuttamām
aṃbhobhir munibhistyaktaiḥ saṃdhyāyāṃ tu niśācarān //
1.54.d:
ऊर्ध्वतश् च करं त्यक्त्वा सभां ब्राह्मीमनुत्तमाम्
अंभोभिर् मुनिभिस्त्यक्तैः संध्यायां तु निशाचरान् ॥
1.54.m: and casting upward a ray towards the supreme assembly of Brahmā, / [and assisted by] the waters offered at twilight by the sages, having struck down the night-wanderers,

1.54.s:
hatvā hatvā tu samprāptān brāhmaṇaiścarate raviḥ
aṣṭādaśa muhūrtaṃ tu uttarāyaṇapaścimam //
1.54.d:
हत्वा हत्वा तु सम्प्राप्तान् ब्राह्मणैश्चरते रविः
अष्टादश मुहूर्तं तु उत्तरायणपश्चिमम् ॥
1.54.m: striking down those who have arrived, the sun moves along with the brāhmaṇas. / The day at the end of the northern course lasts eighteen muhūrtas,

1.54.s:
aharbhavati taccāpi carate mandavikramaḥ
trayodaśārdham ṛkṣāṇi naktaṃ dvādaśabhī raviḥ
muhūrtais tāvad ṛkṣāṇi divāṣṭādaśabhiścaran //
1.54.d:
अहर्भवति तच्चापि चरते मन्दविक्रमः
त्रयोदशार्धम् ऋक्षाणि नक्तं द्वादशभी रविः
मुहूर्तैस् तावद् ऋक्षाणि दिवाष्टादशभिश्चरन् ॥
1.54.m: and during that time too he moves with slow progress. / Traversing thirteen and a half asterisms in the night of twelve muhūrtas, / the sun traverses that same number of asterisms during the day of eighteen muhūrtas.

1.54.s:
tato mandataraṃ nābhyāṃ cakraṃ bhramati vai yathā
mṛtpiṇḍa iva madhyastho dhruvo bhramati vai tathā //
1.54.d:
ततो मन्दतरं नाभ्यां चक्रं भ्रमति वै यथा
मृत्पिण्ड इव मध्यस्थो ध्रुवो भ्रमति वै तथा ॥
1.54.m: Just as the wheel revolves more slowly near the navel, / so Dhruva, standing in the centre like a lump of clay, revolves indeed.

1.54.s:
triṃśanmuhūrtair evāhur ahorātraṃ purāvidaḥ
ubhayoḥ kāṣṭhayormadhye bhramato maṇḍalāni tu //
1.54.d:
त्रिंशन्मुहूर्तैर् एवाहुर् अहोरात्रं पुराविदः
उभयोः काष्ठयोर्मध्ये भ्रमतो मण्डलानि तु ॥
1.54.m: The knowers of antiquity have declared that a day and night consists of thirty muhūrtas; / his circuits revolve between the two limits.

1.54.s:
kulālacakranābhistu yathā tatraiva vartate
auttānapādo bhramati grahaiḥ sārdhaṃ grahāgraṇīḥ //
1.54.d:
कुलालचक्रनाभिस्तु यथा तत्रैव वर्तते
औत्तानपादो भ्रमति ग्रहैः सार्धं ग्रहाग्रणीः ॥
1.54.m: Just as the hub of a potter's wheel remains in that very place, / so the son of Uttānapāda (Dhruva), the leader of the planets, revolves along with the planets.

1.54.s:
gaṇo munijyotiṣāṃ tu manasā tasya sarpati
adhiṣṭhitaḥ punastena bhānustvādāya tiṣṭhati //
1.54.d:
गणो मुनिज्योतिषां तु मनसा तस्य सर्पति
अधिष्ठितः पुनस्तेन भानुस्त्वादाय तिष्ठति ॥
1.54.m: The host of stellar sages glides according to his thought; / and established by him, the sun stays gathering [moisture].

1.54.s:
kiraṇaiḥ sarvatastoyaṃ devo vai sasamīraṇaḥ
auttānapādasya sadā dhruvatvaṃ vai prasādataḥ //
1.54.d:
किरणैः सर्वतस्तोयं देवो वै ससमीरणः
औत्तानपादस्य सदा ध्रुवत्वं वै प्रसादतः ॥
1.54.m: The deity, together with the wind, [draws] water with his rays from everywhere. / The steadfastness (dhruvatva) of the son of Uttānapāda is always by the grace

1.54.s:
viṣṇorauttānapādena cāptaṃ tātasya hetunā
āpaḥ pītāstu sūryeṇa kramante śaśinaḥ kramāt //
1.54.d:
विष्णोरौत्तानपादेन चाप्तं तातस्य हेतुना
आपः पीतास्तु सूर्येण क्रमन्ते शशिनः क्रमात् ॥
1.54.m: of Viṣṇu, attained by the son of Uttānapāda for the sake of his father. / The waters drunk by the sun gradually pass into the moon.

1.54.s:
niśākarānnisravante jīmūtānpratyapaḥ kramāt
vṛndaṃ jalamucāṃ caiva śvasanenābhitāḍitam //
1.54.d:
निशाकरान्निस्रवन्ते जीमूतान्प्रत्यपः क्रमात्
वृन्दं जलमुचां चैव श्वसनेनाभिताडितम् ॥
1.54.m: From the maker of night the waters gradually flow down to the clouds; / and the collection of rain-clouds, struck all around by the wind,

1.54.s:
kṣmāyāṃ sṛṣṭiṃ visṛjate 'bhāsayattena bhāskaraḥ
toyasya nāsti vai nāśaḥ tadaiva parivartate //
1.54.d:
क्ष्मायां सृष्टिं विसृजते ऽभासयत्तेन भास्करः
तोयस्य नास्ति वै नाशः तदैव परिवर्तते ॥
1.54.m: pours forth rain upon the earth; thereby the sun illumines [the world]. / Indeed, there is no destruction of water; it merely circulates continuously.

1.54.s:
hitāya sarvajantūnāṃ gatiḥ śarveṇa nirmitā
bhūrbhuvaḥ svas tathā hyāpo hy annaṃ cāmṛtameva ca //
1.54.d:
हिताय सर्वजन्तूनां गतिः शर्वेण निर्मिता
भूर्भुवः स्वस् तथा ह्यापो ह्य् अन्नं चामृतमेव च ॥
1.54.m: For the benefit of all living beings, the course was fashioned by Śarva: / the earth, midspace, heaven, and likewise the waters, food, and nectar.

1.54.s:
prāṇā vai jagatāmāpo bhūtāni bhuvanāni ca
bahunātra kimuktena carācaramidaṃ jagat //
1.54.d:
प्राणा वै जगतामापो भूतानि भुवनानि च
बहुनात्र किमुक्तेन चराचरमिदं जगत् ॥
1.54.m: Waters indeed are the life-breaths of worlds, the creatures, and the realms; / what need to say much here? They are this moving and unmoving universe.

1.54.s:
apāṃ śivasya bhagavān ādhipatye vyavasthitaḥ
apāṃ tvadhipatirdevo bhava ityeva kīrtitaḥ //
1.54.d:
अपां शिवस्य भगवान् आधिपत्ये व्यवस्थितः
अपां त्वधिपतिर्देवो भव इत्येव कीर्तितः ॥
1.54.m: The Lord is established in the sovereignty over the waters of Śiva; / indeed, the god who is the lord of waters is glorified as Bhava.

1.54.s:
bhavātmakaṃ jagatsarvam iti kiṃ ceha cādbhutam
nārāyaṇatvaṃ devasya hareścādbhiḥ kṛtaṃ vibhoḥ
jagatāmālayo viṣṇus tv āpastasyālayāni tu //
1.54.d:
भवात्मकं जगत्सर्वम् इति किं चेह चाद्भुतम्
नारायणत्वं देवस्य हरेश्चाद्भिः कृतं विभोः
जगतामालयो विष्णुस् त्व् आपस्तस्यालयानि तु ॥
1.54.m: The entire universe consists of Bhava, so what is there to marvel at here? / The lord Hari's state of being Nārāyaṇa was made through the waters by the omnipresent [Śiva]; / Viṣṇu is the abode of the worlds, but the waters are his abode.

1.54.s:
dandahyamāneṣu carācareṣu godhūmabhūtās tvathaniṣkramanti
yā yā ūrdhvaṃ māruteneritā vai tāstāstvabhrāṇyagninā vāyunā ca //
1.54.d:
दन्दह्यमानेषु चराचरेषु गोधूमभूतास् त्वथनिष्क्रमन्ति
या या ऊर्ध्वं मारुतेनेरिता वै तास्तास्त्वभ्राण्यग्निना वायुना च ॥
1.54.m: When moving and unmoving things are consumed by burning, they emerge turned into smoke; / whichever are impelled upward by the wind, those become clouds through fire and wind.

1.54.s:
ato dhūmāgnivātānāṃ saṃyogastvabhramucyate
vārīṇi varṣatītyabhram abhrasyeśaḥ sahasradṛk //
1.54.d:
अतो धूमाग्निवातानां संयोगस्त्वभ्रमुच्यते
वारीणि वर्षतीत्यभ्रम् अभ्रस्येशः सहस्रदृक् ॥
1.54.m: Therefore, the union of smoke, fire, and wind is called a cloud; / that which rains waters (vāri) is a cloud (abhra); the thousand-eyed one is the lord of the cloud.

1.54.s:
yajñadhūmodbhavaṃ cāpi dvijānāṃ hitakṛtsadā
dāvāgnidhūmasambhūtam abhraṃ vanahitaṃ smṛtam //
1.54.d:
यज्ञधूमोद्भवं चापि द्विजानां हितकृत्सदा
दावाग्निधूमसम्भूतम् अभ्रं वनहितं स्मृतम् ॥
1.54.m: And that which arises from the smoke of sacrifice is always beneficial to the twice-born; / the cloud produced from the smoke of a forest fire is considered beneficial to the forest.

1.54.s:
mṛtadhūmodbhavaṃ tvabhram aśubhāya bhaviṣyati
abhicārāgnidhūmotthaṃ bhūtanāśāya vai dvijāḥ //
1.54.d:
मृतधूमोद्भवं त्वभ्रम् अशुभाय भविष्यति
अभिचाराग्निधूमोत्थं भूतनाशाय वै द्विजाः ॥
1.54.m: A cloud arising from the smoke of corpses will bring misfortune; / that rising from the smoke of fire used in malevolent sorcery brings destruction to creatures, O twice-born.

1.54.s:
evaṃ dhūmaviśeṣeṇa jagatāṃ vai hitāhitam
tasmādācchādayeddhūmam abhicārakṛtaṃ naraḥ //
1.54.d:
एवं धूमविशेषेण जगतां वै हिताहितम्
तस्मादाच्छादयेद्धूमम् अभिचारकृतं नरः ॥
1.54.m: Thus, according to the distinction of the smoke, good or evil comes to the worlds; / therefore a man should conceal smoke produced by sorcery.

1.54.s:
anāchādya dvijaḥ kuryād dhūmaṃ yaścābhicārikam
evamuddiśya lokasya kṣayakṛcca bhaviṣyati //
1.54.d:
अनाछाद्य द्विजः कुर्याद् धूमं यश्चाभिचारिकम्
एवमुद्दिश्य लोकस्य क्षयकृच्च भविष्यति ॥
1.54.m: A twice-born man who produces sorcerous smoke without concealing it, / intending it thus, will bring about the ruin of the world.

1.54.s:
apāṃ nidhānaṃ jīmūtāḥ ṣaṇmāsāniha suvratāḥ
varṣayantyeva jagatāṃ hitāya pavanājñayā //
1.54.d:
अपां निधानं जीमूताः षण्मासानिह सुव्रताः
वर्षयन्त्येव जगतां हिताय पवनाज्ञया ॥
1.54.m: The clouds are the storehouse of waters; for six months here, O men of good vows, / they pour down rain for the benefit of the worlds at the command of the wind.

1.54.s:
stanitaṃ ceha vāyavyaṃ vaidyutaṃ pāvakodbhavam
tridhā teṣāmihotpattir abhrāṇāṃ munipuṅgavāḥ //
1.54.d:
स्तनितं चेह वायव्यं वैद्युतं पावकोद्भवम्
त्रिधा तेषामिहोत्पत्तिर् अभ्राणां मुनिपुङ्गवाः ॥
1.54.m: Thunder here is born of the wind; lightning is produced from fire; / threefold is the origin of these clouds here, O best of sages:

1.54.s:
na bhraśyanti yato 'bhrāṇi mehanānmegha ucyate
kāṣṭhāvāhāś ca vairiñcyāḥ pakṣāścaiva pṛthagvidhāḥ //
1.54.d:
न भ्रश्यन्ति यतो ऽभ्राणि मेहनान्मेघ उच्यते
काष्ठावाहाश् च वैरिञ्च्याः पक्षाश्चैव पृथग्विधाः ॥
1.54.m: because they do not fall down (na bhraśyanti), they are called abhra; because of discharging (mehana), they are called megha; / their distinct varieties are: the wooden-bearing, those of Viriñca, and those born of wings.

1.54.s:
ājyānāṃ kāṣṭhasaṃyogād agnerdhūmaḥ pravartitaḥ
dvitīyānāṃ ca saṃbhūtir viriñcocchvāsavāyunā //
1.54.d:
आज्यानां काष्ठसंयोगाद् अग्नेर्धूमः प्रवर्तितः
द्वितीयानां च संभूतिर् विरिञ्चोच्छ्वासवायुना ॥
1.54.m: Smoke of fire is set in motion from the contact of clarified butter with wood; / the origin of the second kind is through the breath-wind of Viriñca;

1.54.s:
bhūbhṛtāṃ tvatha pakṣaistu maghavaccheditaistataḥ
vāhneyāstvatha jīmūtās tv āvahasthānagāḥ śubhāḥ //
1.54.d:
भूभृतां त्वथ पक्षैस्तु मघवच्छेदितैस्ततः
वाह्नेयास्त्वथ जीमूतास् त्व् आवहस्थानगाः शुभाः ॥
1.54.m: and [the third] through the wings of the mountains cut off by Maghavan. / The clouds born of fire, moving in the station of the Āvaha wind, are auspicious;

1.54.s:
viriñcocchvāsajāḥ sarve pravahaskandhajāstataḥ
pakṣajāḥ puṣkarādyāś ca varṣanti ca yadā jalam //
1.54.d:
विरिञ्चोच्छ्वासजाः सर्वे प्रवहस्कन्धजास्ततः
पक्षजाः पुष्कराद्याश् च वर्षन्ति च यदा जलम् ॥
1.54.m: all those born from the breath of Viriñca arise from the shoulder of the Pravaha wind; / and when the wing-born clouds, Puṣkara and the others, pour down water,

1.54.s:
mūkāḥ saśabdaduṣṭāśās tv etaiḥ kṛtyaṃ yathākramam
kṣāmavṛṣṭipradā dīrghakālaṃ śītasamīriṇaḥ //
1.54.d:
मूकाः सशब्ददुष्टाशास् त्व् एतैः कृत्यं यथाक्रमम्
क्षामवृष्टिप्रदा दीर्घकालं शीतसमीरिणः ॥
1.54.m: silent, noisy, and ill-omened, their effect is according to their order: / giving scanty rain for a long time, accompanied by cold winds,

1.54.s:
jīvakāś ca tathā kṣīṇā vidyuddhvanivivarjitāḥ
tiṣṭhantyākrośamātre tu dharāpṛṣṭhāditastataḥ //
1.54.d:
जीवकाश् च तथा क्षीणा विद्युद्ध्वनिविवर्जिताः
तिष्ठन्त्याक्रोशमात्रे तु धरापृष्ठादितस्ततः ॥
1.54.m: and life-giving, yet thin and devoid of lightning and thunder. / They stand at a distance of merely a krośa from the surface of the earth, scattered here and there;

1.54.s:
ardhakrośe tu sarve vai jīmūtā girivāsinaḥ
meghā yojanamātraṃ tu sādhyatvād bahutoyadāḥ //
1.54.d:
अर्धक्रोशे तु सर्वे वै जीमूता गिरिवासिनः
मेघा योजनमात्रं तु साध्यत्वाद् बहुतोयदाः ॥
1.54.m: all mountain-dwelling clouds indeed stand at half a krośa; / clouds that are at a mere yojana yield abundant water because of their tractability,

1.54.s:
dharāpṛṣṭhāddvijāḥ kṣmāyāṃ vidyudguṇasamanvitāḥ
teṣāṃ teṣāṃ vṛṣṭisargaṃ tredhā kathitamatra tu //
1.54.d:
धरापृष्ठाद्द्विजाः क्ष्मायां विद्युद्गुणसमन्विताः
तेषां तेषां वृष्टिसर्गं त्रेधा कथितमत्र तु ॥
1.54.m: above the surface of the earth, O twice-born, endowed with the quality of lightning over the ground; / their creation of rain has been proclaimed threefold here.

1.54.s:
pakṣajāḥ kalpajāḥ sarve parvatānāṃ mahattamāḥ
kalpānte te ca varṣanti rātrau nāśāya śāradāḥ //
1.54.d:
पक्षजाः कल्पजाः सर्वे पर्वतानां महत्तमाः
कल्पान्ते ते च वर्षन्ति रात्रौ नाशाय शारदाः ॥
1.54.m: All the wing-born clouds are born at the end of a kalpa, greatest among mountains; / at the end of a kalpa they pour down rain at night for destruction, being autumnal.

1.54.s:
pakṣajāḥ puṣkarādyāś ca varṣanti ca yadā jalam
tadārṇavamabhūtsarvaṃ tatra śete niśīśvaraḥ //
1.54.d:
पक्षजाः पुष्कराद्याश् च वर्षन्ति च यदा जलम्
तदार्णवमभूत्सर्वं तत्र शेते निशीश्वरः ॥
1.54.m: And when the wing-born clouds, Puṣkara and the rest, pour down water, / then everything becomes an ocean, and therein sleeps the lord of the night.

1.54.s:
āgneyānāṃ śvāsajānāṃ pakṣajānāṃ dvijarṣabhāḥ
jaladānāṃ sadā dhūmo hy āpyāyana iti smṛtaḥ //
1.54.d:
आग्नेयानां श्वासजानां पक्षजानां द्विजर्षभाः
जलदानां सदा धूमो ह्य् आप्यायन इति स्मृतः ॥
1.54.m: For clouds born of fire, born of breath, and born of wings, O best of the twice-born, / smoke is always traditionally known as that which nourishes them.

1.54.s:
pauṇḍrāstu vṛṣṭayaḥ sarvā vaidyutāḥ śītaśasyadāḥ
puṇḍradeśeṣu patitā nāgānāṃ śīkarā himāḥ //
1.54.d:
पौण्ड्रास्तु वृष्टयः सर्वा वैद्युताः शीतशस्यदाः
पुण्ड्रदेशेषु पतिता नागानां शीकरा हिमाः ॥
1.54.m: All the Pauṇḍra rains are full of lightning, yielding cold-season crops; / the icy sprays of the serpents have fallen in the Puṇḍra regions.

1.54.s:
gāṅgā gaṅgāmbusambhūtā parjanyena parāvahaiḥ
nagānāṃ ca nadīnāṃ ca diggajānāṃ samākulam //
1.54.d:
गाङ्गा गङ्गाम्बुसम्भूता पर्जन्येन परावहैः
नगानां च नदीनां च दिग्गजानां समाकुलम् ॥
1.54.m: The Gāṅga rains are born from the water of the Gaṅgā by Parjanya via the Parāvaha winds; / bringing turmoil to mountains, rivers, and directional elephants,

1.54.s:
meghānāṃ ca pṛthagbhūtaṃ jalaṃ prāyādagādagam
parāvaho yaḥ śvasanaś cānayatyambikāgurum //
1.54.d:
मेघानां च पृथग्भूतं जलं प्रायादगादगम्
परावहो यः श्वसनश् चानयत्यम्बिकागुरुम् ॥
1.54.m: the water, divided among the clouds, goes from mountain to mountain. / The wind that is Parāvaha brings [clouds to] the father of Ambikā;

1.54.s:
menāpatimatikramya vṛṣṭiśeṣaṃ dvijāḥ param
abhyeti bhārate varṣe tv aparāntavivṛddhaye //
1.54.d:
मेनापतिमतिक्रम्य वृष्टिशेषं द्विजाः परम्
अभ्येति भारते वर्षे त्व् अपरान्तविवृद्धये ॥
1.54.m: passing beyond the husband of Menā, O twice-born, the great residue of the rain / comes to the realm of Bhārata for the increase of the western borderland.

1.54.s:
vṛṣṭayaḥ kathitā hyadya dvidhā vastu vivṛddhaye
sasyadvayasya saṃkṣepāt prabravīmi yathāmati //
1.54.d:
वृष्टयः कथिता ह्यद्य द्विधा वस्तु विवृद्धये
सस्यद्वयस्य संक्षेपात् प्रब्रवीमि यथामति ॥
